records.definition: A physical device worn on the genitals to prevent sexual intercourse, erection, or masturbation, used in BDSM power exchange or orgasm control.
records.notes: Historically associated with the largely-mythologized medieval chastity belt; modern devices are a commercially significant product category with mainstream retail presence.

records.definition: Crude slang for a male chastity cage: a device that encases the penis to prevent erection or sexual activity, used in BDSM orgasm control dynamics.

records.definition: A dated American euphemism for a brothel.
records.notes: Primarily 19th–early 20th century American; derives from 'sporting life,' the milieu of gamblers, criminals, and prostitutes.

records.definition: A dated American euphemism for a prostitute.
records.notes: Part of the 'sporting life' euphemistic cluster; 19th–early 20th century American South and West.

records.definition: A dated term for a man's mistress or kept woman.
records.notes: Occasionally extended to mean prostitute; 19th–mid 20th century; faintly humorous or affectionate in modern use.

records.definition: To perform anal intercourse upon someone; derived from the archaic legal term sodomy.
records.notes: Retains use in journalism and law; British variant 'sodomise'; carries moral weight absent from clinical 'anal intercourse'.

records.definition: An archaic and pejorative term for a person, especially a gay man, who practices sodomy.
records.notes: Derived from the biblical city of Sodom; primarily a religious/moral condemnation; still used in some conservative religious contexts.

records.definition: An archaic legal and moral term for sodomy or other non-procreative sexual acts.
records.notes: Legal framing that pathologizes non-normative sexuality as contrary to nature; used in criminal statutes into the late 20th century.

records.definition: An archaic American legal term for sodomy or other non-procreative sexual acts.
records.notes: Appeared in US state statutes until Lawrence v. Texas (2003) invalidated such laws; more prevalent in American than British legal tradition.

records.definition: A legal term for a sexual act that violates community standards of decency.
records.notes: Broader than sodomy laws; covers public exposure, lewdness, and similar offenses; still in some active legal usage.

records.definition: Sexually offensive behavior or material that violates standards of public decency.
records.notes: Still active in legal and regulatory contexts (e.g., FCC broadcast indecency rules); higher recognition reflects ongoing legal currency.

records.definition: Sexually explicit material that lacks serious artistic, literary, political, or scientific value.
records.notes: Has a precise US legal definition (Miller test, 1973); also used colloquially for strong profanity; one of the more technically alive 'archaic' legal terms.

records.definition: Referring to sexual or scatological matters in a crude but humorously irreverent way.
records.notes: More literary register than 'bawdy'; often used to characterize comedic traditions (Chaucer, Rabelais, Aristophanes); implies appreciative rather than condemnatory tone.

records.definition: Excessive or offensive sexual desire combined with active predatory pursuit.
records.notes: Implies active pursuit and moral censure beyond mere 'lust'; see also 'lecher' (the person who enacts it).

records.definition: The quality of being sexually immoral or unrestrained in behavior.
records.notes: Stronger moral condemnation than 'promiscuity'; implies deliberate rejection of sexual norms; related forms: licentious (adj).

records.definition: A person, especially a man, who freely pursues sexual pleasure without moral restraint.
records.notes: Originally a freed slave, then a religious freethinker; sexual sense dominant by 17th century; can carry admiration or condemnation depending on context.

records.definition: An archaic term for a man of dissolute habits who irresponsibly pursues sexual pleasure.
records.notes: Short for 'rakehell'; prominent in Restoration and 18th-century literature (Hogarth's 'A Rake's Progress'); carries a romanticized male archetype quality.

records.definition: A debauched or licentious man, especially one of high social standing.
records.notes: French loanword literally meaning 'broken on the wheel'; implies higher social class and more deliberate hedonism than English 'rake'; accent mark often dropped in English usage.

records.definition: An archaic term for debauchery or a scene of disorderly sexual excess.
records.notes: Extremely rare in this sense; almost entirely displaced by 'rout' meaning military defeat; extremely high risk of misinterpretation without context.

records.definition: A love affair, especially one that is secret or illicit.
records.notes: French loanword; carries connotations of secrecy, passion, and Continental sophistication that 'love affair' alone does not fully convey; see also 'amorous'.

records.definition: A lover, especially one in a secret or illicit relationship; often implies an adulterous partner.
records.notes: Implies illicit or adulterous context; from Old French 'par amour' (by love); the word itself carries more romantic weight than 'mistress'.

records.definition: A woman with whom one is romantically or sexually in love; a female beloved or lover.
records.notes: Italian loanword; gendered form distinguishes it from neutral 'lover'; rarely used outside literary or deliberately florid speech.

records.definition: A man with whom one is romantically or sexually in love; a male beloved or lover.
records.notes: Italian loanword; masculine counterpart to inamorata; rarer in English usage even than its feminine pair.

records.definition: A young male admirer or suitor, especially in pastoral poetry; a rustic lover.
records.notes: Strongly pastoral connotation; also historically meant 'young man' or 'rustic youth'; virtually unused outside period literature today.

records.definition: One who courts or seeks the romantic or sexual affection of another person.
records.notes: Derived from the verb 'woo'; more widely understood than swain because 'woo' remains in casual use; felt archaic but not opaque.

records.definition: A persistent and often painful penile erection unrelated to sexual arousal, considered a urological emergency.
records.notes: Named after Priapus; recognition boosted by ED drug warnings (e.g. Viagra); not dated — it remains the active clinical term.

records.definition: Greek and Roman god of fertility depicted with a permanent oversized erection; protector of gardens and livestock.
records.notes: Eponym of priapism; his image (a herm with erect phallus) was used as a garden boundary marker in antiquity; appears in classical literature and art history.

records.definition: Roman goddess of love, beauty, and sexuality; used as an archetype or symbol of female sexual beauty and desire.
records.notes: Planet name dominates modern recognition; 'venereal' (as in venereal disease) and 'venery' derive from her name; sexual connotation secondary for most speakers today.

records.definition: A food, substance, or stimulus believed to arouse or intensify sexual desire.
records.notes: Derived from Aphrodite; widely used in modern English with no dated feel; scientific evidence for most claimed aphrodisiacs is thin.

records.definition: Having strong masculine qualities, especially vigorous sexual potency or physical vitality.
records.notes: From Latin 'virilis' (of a man); conflates sexual potency with general physical strength; carries faint ideological charge around masculinity.

records.definition: The quality or state of being virile; male sexual potency and physical vigor.
records.notes: Nominal form of virile; often invoked in discussions of testosterone, fertility, and masculinity ideology; slightly literary in feel.

records.definition: The capacity for sexual performance, especially the ability to achieve and sustain an erection.
records.notes: Has broad non-sexual meanings (strength, concentration, drug dosage); sexual meaning is understood only in context; not inherently dated.

records.definition: Unable to achieve or sustain an erection; also used pejoratively to mean helpless or without power.
records.notes: Clinical use largely displaced by 'erectile dysfunction' since the 1990s; persists as a pejorative insult in non-sexual contexts (e.g. 'impotent rage').

records.definition: The inability to achieve or maintain an erection sufficient for sexual intercourse; formerly the standard clinical term.
records.notes: Largely replaced by 'erectile dysfunction' in clinical and advertising contexts since the mid-1990s Viagra era; still widely understood.

records.definition: Intense, often overwhelming sexual desire or appetite.
records.notes: One of the seven deadly sins in Christian tradition; used across all registers from theology to casual speech; carries moral-transgressive freight that 'desire' does not.

records.definition: Filled with or characterized by strong sexual desire; lustful.
records.notes: From 'concupiscence'; primarily a theological word; rarely encountered outside academic, religious, or deliberately archaic texts.

records.definition: Curvaceous and sexually attractive; suggesting or devoted to sensual pleasure.
records.notes: Originally applicable to any sensual pleasure; now almost exclusively applied to women's bodies; implies a full, curved figure; slightly literary but not uncommon.

records.definition: Lecherous; having or showing an excessive desire for sexual gratification.
records.notes: Variant of 'licorous'; historically also meant eager for food or drink; the sexual sense is now the only sense most speakers would guess at; deeply obsolete.

records.definition: Treating sexual matters in an indecent, titillating, or prurient way.
records.notes: Describes content or manner rather than desire itself; favored in literary criticism and tabloid journalism; slightly archaic but still encountered.

records.definition: Excessive or unhealthy interest in sexual matters, especially of a voyeuristic or indecent nature.
records.notes: Has a specific legal meaning in US obscenity law ('prurient interest' from Miller v. California, 1973); the legal usage keeps it alive in educated registers.

records.definition: Having or exhibiting excessive sexual desire; driven by the libido.
records.notes: From Latin 'libido'; the psychoanalytic lineage lends it a pseudo-clinical edge; used more in literary or ironic contexts than in conversation.

records.definition: Feeling or showing romantic or sexual love and desire.
records.notes: Blends romantic and sexual desire without privileging either; softer and more courtly than 'lustful'; still encountered in literary and semi-formal contexts.

records.definition: Acronym for 'that hoe over there'; a derogatory label for a woman deemed sexually promiscuous.
records.notes: Originated in AAVE and hip-hop; peaked in mainstream internet usage 2014–2016; carries stronger race-class coding than 'slut'; slightly dated by 2026 but still widely recognized.

records.definition: A man who is excessively deferential or attentive toward women in hopes of romantic or sexual attention that is not reciprocated.
records.notes: Popularized on TikTok and in incel/gaming subcultures ca. 2020; implies the man's devotion is unearned and exploitable; now mainstream enough to have lost much subculture specificity.

records.definition: Short for cuckold; an internet insult for a man perceived as weak, emasculated, or whose partner is sexually unfaithful.
records.notes: Weaponized as a political insult in 2016 US election cycle ('cuckservative'); has simultaneous roots in Elizabethan drama and the modern cuckolding kink community, creating an ironic double meaning.

records.definition: A man who is unable to find a sexual or romantic partner despite wanting one, often associated with online communities marked by resentment and misogyny.
records.notes: Coined 1997 by a Canadian woman; reclaimed and politicized by male communities post-2010; associated with radicalization and several mass-casualty events.

records.definition: A man who pursues casual sex while being emotionally unavailable, dishonest, or manipulative toward partners.
records.notes: Rose to prominence circa 2014–2016 via social media; also spelled fuckboi; older prison slang meaning differed (a submissive male used sexually by others).

records.definition: Abbreviated form of fuckboy; a sexually exploitative and emotionally irresponsible man.
records.notes: Sanitized abbreviation enabling use in censored or broadcast contexts; shares concept slug with fuckboy.

records.definition: A sexually permissive person, typically a woman; used as an insult but partially reclaimed in AAVE and hip-hop culture.
records.notes: AAVE origin; pervasive in hip-hop since 1990s; increasingly gender-neutral in internet usage; phonetic respelling of whore but treated as a distinct lexical item.

records.definition: To have sex with someone, typically implying a casual or vigorous encounter.
records.notes: Popularized by the smash-or-pass meme format; crude level is moderate — blunt but not anatomical; also used in gaming contexts with no sexual meaning.

records.definition: To send a private message to someone on social media with romantic or sexual intent, often after publicly engaging with their content.
records.notes: DMs = direct messages; peaked approximately 2016–2017 on Twitter and Instagram; still understood but now slightly dated as a novel phrase.

records.definition: The male anus framed as a penetrable orifice; portmanteau of boy and pussy, originating in AAVE and gay male communities.
records.notes: Primarily used in gay male and queer contexts; spread to broader internet culture via meme communities; carries playful rather than purely pejorative tone.

records.definition: To ejaculate (verb) or semen (noun); originating in AAVE and widely adopted across hip-hop and internet slang.
records.notes: AAVE origin; polysemous (nuts = testicles in a separate, milder usage); extremely common in online sexual discourse and explicit music lyrics.

records.definition: Not Safe For Work; a content warning tag indicating sexually explicit, graphic, or otherwise inappropriate material.
records.notes: Originated in early internet and forum culture circa early 2000s; near-universal across English-speaking internet; antonym SFW (safe for work) also common.

records.definition: A deliberately sexualized photo or video posted on social media to attract desire, attention, or validation from viewers.
records.notes: Requires knowledge of thirsty (sexually desirous sense) to fully decode; became mainstream Instagram and TikTok vocabulary circa 2018–2020.

records.definition: Desperately eager for sexual or romantic attention in a way that reads as needy or off-putting.
records.notes: Semantic shift extending the physical-thirst metaphor; widely understood across age groups; can be self-deprecating or critical depending on context.

records.definition: To receive far more replies than likes on a social media post, signaling community rejection; deployed in sexual shaming contexts when someone's behavior or hypocrisy is publicly condemned.
records.notes: Not inherently sexual; included for its role in online sexual shaming dynamics; peaked on Twitter circa 2020–2021; recognition drops sharply among non-Twitter users.

records.definition: To publicly reveal someone's sexual images, messages, or behavior without their consent, typically as retaliation or shaming.
records.notes: Verbal form; closely linked to leaked nudes and revenge porn phenomena; used as a threat in phrases like I will expose you; also used in non-sexual scandal contexts.

records.definition: Nude or sexually explicit photographs or videos of a person distributed without that person's consent.
records.notes: Focuses on content and mechanism (the leak); gained mainstream prominence after the 2014 celebrity iCloud breach; shares concept slug with revenge porn, which emphasizes perpetrator motive.

records.definition: The non-consensual distribution of intimate or sexually explicit images of a person, typically by a former partner as retaliation.
records.notes: Now a legal term in many jurisdictions; preferred clinical term is non-consensual intimate image sharing (NCII); shares concept slug with leaked nudes.

records.definition: To create a false online identity in order to deceive someone into a romantic or sexual relationship.
records.notes: Popularized by the 2010 documentary and subsequent MTV series; motivations include sexual access, emotional manipulation, or financial fraud; used as both verb and noun.

records.definition: The act of abruptly cutting off all communication with a romantic or sexual partner without explanation.
records.notes: Mainstream enough to appear in major dictionaries; strongly associated with dating app culture; also used in platonic and professional contexts, diluting the sexual specificity.

records.definition: The practice of sending intermittent flirtatious or affectionate signals to someone without any intention of committing to a relationship.
records.notes: Metaphor from the Hansel and Gretel breadcrumb trail; popularized in dating advice media circa 2017; less mainstream than ghosting; recognition concentrated among active dating-app users.

records.definition: An undefined romantic or sexual relationship that has the qualities of a committed partnership but lacks explicit labels or mutual commitment.
records.notes: Portmanteau of situation and relationship; popularized on TikTok circa 2021–2023; fills a genuine lexical gap for ambiguous modern relationship structures that predate the term.

records.definition: A relationship between two friends who engage in sexual activity without romantic commitment or exclusivity.
records.notes: Sufficiently mainstream to title two major Hollywood films (2011); euphemistic in that benefits is a coded reference to sex; widely understood across generations and regions.

records.definition: Abbreviation for friends with benefits; a sexual relationship between friends without romantic commitment.
records.notes: Primarily used in dating app bios, personal ads, and online forums; shares concept slug with full form.

records.definition: Abbreviation for one-night stand; a single sexual encounter with no expectation of ongoing contact.
records.notes: Somewhat more common in UK English dating contexts and personal ads than in American usage; shares concept slug with one-night stand.

records.definition: A sexual encounter between two people spanning a single occasion with no intention of meeting again for sex.
records.notes: Decades-old idiom with theatrical origin (a one-night performance stop on a tour); mainstream and widely used across all English-speaking regions.

records.definition: A social pattern, particularly among young adults and on college campuses, characterized by casual sexual encounters without expectation of commitment.
records.notes: Used analytically in academic sociology as well as popular discourse; hookup alone refers to a specific encounter while hookup culture describes the broader norm.

records.definition: A sexual arrangement in which both parties agree there is no emotional commitment, exclusivity, or expectation of a continuing relationship.
records.notes: General idiom applied to many non-sexual contexts (gifts, business deals) but immediately understood in sexual contexts; abbreviated NSA in personal ads; also a 2011 film title.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'no strings attached,' indicating a sexual or romantic arrangement with no expectation of emotional commitment or exclusivity.
records.notes: Ambiguous out of context (also National Security Agency); meaning as a dating/hookup term is primary on apps and personals.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'down to fuck'; signals immediate willingness to engage in casual sex.
records.notes: Popularized by early Tinder and hookup app culture; still in use but peak was early 2010s dating app discourse.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'drug and disease free,' used in hookup profiles and personal ads to signal STI-negative and non-drug-using status.
records.notes: Common in gay hookup app culture (Grindr, Scruff) and straight personals; carries implicit stigma against those who cannot claim the status; declining as PrEP normalization shifts STI disclosure norms.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'big black cock,' a racially fetishizing pornographic category and personal ad term rooted in racial stereotyping of Black men's genitalia.
records.notes: Racially charged and fetishizing; ubiquitous as a porn category label; widely recognized beyond porn audiences due to internet meme culture; reflects and reinforces racist stereotypes.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'big white cock,' a pornographic category and personal ad term used primarily in interracial adult content contexts.
records.notes: Considerably less ubiquitous than BBC; appears in interracial pornography categories and personal ads; racially frames penis size as a White male attribute.

records.definition: Adjective describing a man as having a large penis.
records.notes: Widely understood across demographics; frequent in personal ads, gay culture, and mainstream media; shares concept with 'well-hung'.

records.definition: Adjective describing a man as having a notably large penis; slightly more emphatic phrasing than 'hung'.
records.notes: Shares concept with 'hung'; marginally more complete or formal phrasing; appears in literature, jokes, and personals; hyphenated form is standard.

records.definition: Internet idiom for an aura of effortless, unforced sexual confidence and charisma, attributed regardless of the subject's actual anatomy or gender.
records.notes: Coined June 2018 following Ariana Grande's tweets about Pete Davidson; rapidly desexualized and applied to people of any gender; Oxford Dictionaries tracked as a notable cultural coinage.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'big dick energy'; the acronym form of the confident-charisma internet idiom.
records.notes: Shares concept with 'big dick energy'; lower recognition than the full phrase outside heavy social media users; crude score lower because explicit term is obscured by acronym.

records.definition: Abbreviation for 'small dick energy,' internet slang for insecure, petty, or overcompensating behavior attributed to someone who feels threatened by others.
records.notes: Coined as antonym of BDE; lower recognition because it is used less frequently; collides with 'subject matter expert' in professional contexts, reducing clarity.

records.definition: A person, typically gay or bisexual, who strongly prefers sexual partners with large penises.
records.notes: Originated in gay male subculture; 'queen' does not imply femininity; used both self-descriptively and as light teasing; not considered a serious slur; has crossed into mainstream LGBTQ+ and dating discourse.

records.definition: A receptive (bottom) sexual partner who takes an active, dominant, or controlling role during anal intercourse, directing pace, position, and intensity.
records.notes: Originated in gay male culture; increasingly recognized in mainstream LGBTQ+ discourse; implies the bottom controls the encounter rather than being passive; sometimes used humorously in non-sexual contexts.

records.definition: Abbreviation of 'versatile'; describes a person willing to take both insertive (top) and receptive (bottom) roles in anal sex.
records.notes: Primarily gay male hookup app terminology (Grindr, Scruff); extended forms 'vers top' and 'vers bottom' indicate preference lean; low crude score because it functions as a near-clinical role descriptor within its community of use.

records.definition: The act of subtly and indirectly introducing a new romantic or sexual partner to one's social media audience without explicit confirmation, typically through partial reveals in photos or stories.
records.notes: Borrowed from business/tech jargon; primarily a TikTok and Instagram cultural phenomenon; peaked in mainstream discourse around 2021-2022; antonym is 'hard launch' (explicit announcement).

records.definition: Gen Z slang for natural charisma and attractive energy, especially the effortless ability to charm or attract romantic and sexual partners.
records.notes: Oxford University Press Word of the Year 2023; etymologically derived from 'charisma' (charisma → chrisma → rizz); popularized by streamer Kai Cenat; used for both sexual attractiveness and general charm.

records.definition: Present participle of 'rizz'; the act of deploying sexual or romantic charisma to attract or charm someone.
records.notes: Verb form of 'rizz'; 'rizzing up' is a common construction (e.g., 'rizzing her up'); shares concept with 'rizz'; slightly lower recognition than the noun form.

records.definition: Idiom meaning to make a romantic or sexual advance on someone despite uncertainty of success; to try one's luck with an attractive person.
records.notes: Basketball metaphor applied to dating; widely used across age groups and platforms; not inherently crude, though context can make it explicitly sexual; shares 'sexual_advance' concept with 'slide'.

records.definition: Internet slang meaning to make a romantic or sexual advance, especially by sending a direct message on social media ('slide into the DMs').
records.notes: Most commonly used in the construction 'slide into someone's DMs'; standalone 'slide' is contextually ambiguous; shares 'sexual_advance' concept with 'shoot your shot'.

records.definition: A significant positive physical transformation that increases a person's attractiveness or sexual appeal, often referring to puberty, weight loss, or personal reinvention.
records.notes: Originated in Black American slang; went mainstream ~2015-2018 via social media; 'glowed up' is the past tense form; low crude score because it refers to physical improvement rather than sexual activity directly.

records.definition: Slang for the total number of sexual partners a person has had, borrowed from the military term for casualties.
records.notes: Morbid metaphor borrowed from war casualty counting; widely used in social media and dating discourse; associated with judgment and slut-shaming disproportionately directed at women; shares concept with 'kill count'.

records.definition: Crude variant of 'body count'; the number of sexual partners a person has had, framed through an aggressive hunting or warfare metaphor.
records.notes: More aggressive and objectifying framing than 'body count' due to the predatory 'kill' metaphor; less commonly used; shares concept with 'body count'; predominantly used by men discussing sexual history.

records.definition: Social anxiety or shame experienced over the number of sexual partners one has had, particularly in the context of anticipated judgment by a current or prospective partner.
records.notes: Compound formed from 'body count'; reflects the cultural shame economy around sexual history; disproportionately affects women who face harsher social judgment for higher counts; frequently discussed in social media dating discourse.

records.definition: Gen Z/millennial adverb meaning 'quietly' or 'secretly,' frequently used to express a concealed or understated sexual or romantic attraction (e.g., 'I low-key want to sleep with him').
records.notes: Not inherently sexual; the sexual meaning is entirely contextual; one of the most versatile pieces of internet slang with extremely high recognition; sexual use is only one of many registers.

records.definition: A romantic and/or sexual relationship that lacks clear definition, commitment, or official status, occupying territory between friendship and an exclusive partnership.
records.notes: Portmanteau of 'situation' and '-ship' (relationship suffix); captures the modern phenomenon of commitment-avoiding arrangements that include sex; widely used in dating app discourse since ~2019-2022.

records.definition: The behavior of continuing to engage with someone's social media content (liking posts, watching stories) after being romantically or sexually rejected or ghosted by them.
records.english_term: lingering social media engagement after rejection
records.notes: Term coined ~2018 in a Man Repeller article as a counterpart to 'ghosting'; the orbital metaphor is apt — maintaining distance while staying in the gravitational field; describes a distinctly post-smartphone dating behavior.

records.definition: The practice of a woman penetrating a man anally using a strap-on dildo.
records.notes: Term coined via a Dan Savage reader contest ca. 2001; internet-native but has crossed into mainstream media.

records.definition: Sex offered out of sympathy or obligation rather than genuine desire.
Sex between two people who dislike or are hostile toward each other, typically intense or emotionally charged.
Sex that occurs after an argument or conflict in a relationship, often framed as reconciliatory.
records.notes: Among the most mainstream terms in this section; appears regularly in sitcoms and non-explicit media.

records.definition: Sex that occurs at or around the dissolution of a romantic relationship.
Sex with a former romantic or sexual partner, not necessarily at or near the time of the breakup.
records.notes: Overlaps with breakup sex but implies greater temporal distance from the end of the relationship.

records.definition: Experiencing sexual or romantic attraction to people regardless of gender identity, with gender not being a determining factor in attraction.
records.notes: Distinguished from bisexual by explicit inclusion of non-binary genders; ongoing community debate about conceptual overlap with bisexuality.

records.definition: A sexual orientation in which attraction is experienced only after forming a significant emotional bond with a person.
records.notes: Coined online ca. 2006; considered part of the asexual (ace) spectrum; mainstream recognition growing but still primarily a community term.

records.definition: A person who is primarily or significantly attracted to others based on perceived intelligence.
records.notes: Had higher cultural profile ca. 2015-2018 when dating apps like OkCupid added it as an orientation option; faced academic and community pushback on whether intelligence attraction constitutes a distinct orientation; recognition now plateaued or slightly declining.

records.definition: An orientation on the asexual spectrum describing people who experience sexual attraction rarely, weakly, or only under specific circumstances.
records.notes: Also spelled greysexual; the gray/grey signals a middle zone between fully asexual and fully sexual; part of the ace spectrum community lexicon.

records.definition: An asexual-spectrum orientation characterized by arousal from sexual fantasies or content in which oneself is absent or a disconnected observer rather than a participant.
records.notes: Also termed autochorissexual (coined by Anthony Bogaert 2012); the aego prefix derives from Greek for without self; recognition almost entirely limited to online ace communities.

records.definition: Informal abbreviation for polyamorous or polyamory; the practice of or openness to multiple consensual romantic or sexual relationships simultaneously.
records.notes: Context-dependent; shares form with non-sexual uses (polyester, polygon) but sexual meaning is unambiguous in community contexts.

records.definition: An umbrella descriptor for any relationship structure involving multiple partners conducted with the full knowledge and consent of all involved.
records.notes: The ethically prefix explicitly distinguishes from cheating; frequently used as a dating-app self-description.

records.definition: Abbreviation for Ethical Non-Monogamy; any consensual multi-partner relationship structure.
records.notes: Common self-descriptor on Feeld, OkCupid, and Hinge; recognition outside polyamory-adjacent communities is low.

records.definition: A relationship philosophy that rejects prescribed hierarchies among romantic, sexual, and platonic connections, treating each relationship on its own unique terms.
records.notes: Concept articulated by Andie Nordgren (Swedish) ca. 2006; the English term is a translation that became canonical in anglophone polyamory communities.

records.definition: The positive feeling of joy or satisfaction experienced when one's partner experiences happiness, pleasure, or love with another person.
records.english_term: vicarious joy from partner's pleasure with another
records.notes: Coined by the Kerista commune (San Francisco) in the 1970s-80s; often described as the opposite of jealousy; no prior English word existed for this emotional state.

records.definition: New Relationship Energy; the intense excitement, idealization, and passion characteristic of the early stage of a new romantic or sexual relationship.
records.notes: Polyamory community term used to describe and manage the infatuation phase, which can disrupt established relationships; analogous to limerence in academic psychology.

records.definition: One's partner's other romantic or sexual partner, with whom one does not share a direct romantic or sexual relationship.
records.notes: Coined within anglophone polyamory communities; no prior English word existed for this specific relational role; recognition is almost entirely limited to polyamory community members.

records.definition: Describing an intimate, committed relationship that is neither conventionally romantic nor purely platonic, typically involving deep emotional closeness without sexual or romantic components.
records.notes: Coined in aromantic and asexual (aro/ace) online communities ca. 2010-2012; abbreviated QPR (queerplatonic relationship); queer here signals deviation from normative relationship categories rather than LGBTQ identity per se.

records.definition: Describing a person who is interested in or practices non-conventional sexual activities, especially BDSM, fetishes, or power exchange.
records.notes: Fully crossed into mainstream usage; appears regularly in non-explicit media; antonym is vanilla.

records.definition: In sexual contexts, describing conventional or non-kinky sexual practices or a person uninterested in BDSM and fetish activities.
records.notes: Extension of general English slang meaning plain or ordinary; widely understood outside kink communities; mildly pejorative within kink communities but not a slur.

records.definition: The act of mocking, criticizing, or expressing disgust at another person's sexual kinks or fetishes.
records.notes: Follows the X-shaming construction (cf. slut-shaming, body-shaming); frames kink judgment as analogous to other forms of social discrimination; internet-native framing.

records.definition: A non-conventional sexual interest, practice, or fetish, often encompassing BDSM and related activities.
records.notes: Highly mainstream as a noun; somewhat less crude than fetish in common usage; cognate adjective is kinky.

records.definition: The act of creating or consuming sexualized fan content depicting a character, particularly one not originally presented as sexual.
records.notes: Gerund of lewd; originates in anime, gaming, and VTuber fan communities; applies to fictional characters and occasionally to public figures; recognized almost exclusively within fan communities.

records.definition: Self-published Japanese fan comics, frequently but not exclusively erotic, typically based on characters from existing anime, manga, or video games.
records.notes: Japanese loanword (同人誌); in English-language usage the term carries a stronger erotic connotation than in Japanese, where it covers all self-published fan works regardless of content; recognized almost entirely within anime and gaming fan communities.

records.definition: Japanese-style animated or illustrated pornography, typically featuring exaggerated anatomy and fantastical scenarios.
records.notes: Loanword from Japanese; in Japanese 変態 means 'pervert' or 'abnormal behavior', not specifically animation; the English sense is narrowed to anime/manga-style explicit content.

records.definition: Internet adage stating that pornographic content exists for any conceivable subject, character, or object.
records.notes: Part of the 'Rules of the Internet'; originated on 4chan circa 2003-2006; cited humorously or to explain the scope of internet pornography; no prior English equivalent as a named rule.

records.definition: To masturbate; internet slang based on an onomatopoeic representation of the act.
records.notes: Originated in the webcomic 'Sexy Losers' (1999); popularized on 4chan and Reddit ca. 2005-2013; also the root of the NoFap abstinence community name.

records.definition: Masturbating; the present participle and gerund form of the internet slang verb 'fap'.
records.notes: Gerund/progressive form of 'fap'; used both as a verb ('I was fapping') and noun ('no fapping').

records.definition: To ejaculate; also used as a noun for semen; in chan culture, shorthand for compulsive pornography-driven masturbation.
records.notes: 4chan slang circa 2018-2020; the 'oo' spelling is a deliberate stylization distinguishing it from 'cum'; associated with the Coomer wojak meme and the critique of pornography addiction.

records.definition: A person, typically male, who is addicted to pornography and masturbation to the point of perceived social and physical degradation.
records.notes: Derived from a wojak meme character depicting a gaunt, hollow-eyed man; used mockingly or self-deprecatingly; the term implies physical deterioration as a consequence of the addiction.

records.notes: Not exclusively sexual; sexual transgression is one common vector alongside violence, racism, and nihilism; used as a pejorative; peaked in usage ca. 2014-2018 on 4chan, Reddit, and Twitter.

records.definition: Acronym for 'Mother I'd Like to Fuck'; a sexually attractive middle-aged or older woman, especially one who is a mother.

records.definition: A young man with an internet-native aesthetic (layered shirts, chains, emo and skater influences) who often maintains a flirtatious online presence.
records.notes: Parallel construction to e-girl; less sexually coded in practice; popularized on TikTok ca. 2019; the aesthetic blends emo, soft-boy, and skater influences.

records.definition: A secondary, private social media account used to share content kept off one's public profile, often sexual, risqué, or otherwise sensitive material.
records.notes: Portmanteau of 'fake' + 'Instagram'; not exclusively sexual but commonly used for explicit content, OnlyFans promotion, or relationship secrets; the term predates but gained mainstream recognition ca. 2016-2019.

records.definition: Abbreviation for OnlyFans, a subscription-based platform widely used for sexual content creation and digital sex work.
records.notes: The abbreviation is used on social media to evade content moderation filters that flag the full platform name; mainstream recognition surged during COVID-era platform growth (2020-2021).

records.definition: The act of sending sexually explicit text messages, images, or videos via mobile device or messaging application.
records.notes: Portmanteau of 'sex' + 'texting'; entered mainstream media and legal discourse ca. 2009-2012; appears in legislation regarding minors in numerous jurisdictions.

records.definition: Nude or sexually explicit photographs of oneself or others, typically shared digitally.
records.notes: Plural noun used as shorthand; appears in legal discourse around non-consensual image sharing and CSAM; the colloquial brevity normalizes the exchange compared to the clinical full form.

records.definition: A photograph of a penis, typically sent digitally and often unsolicited.
records.notes: The unsolicited form has entered legal discourse as sexual harassment; several jurisdictions have criminalized unsolicited sending; the solicited form is central to sexting culture.

records.definition: A provocative or sexualized selfie posted or sent with conscious intent to attract romantic or sexual attention.
records.notes: Related to 'thirst trap' (a post engineered to elicit 'thirsty' responses); the sender is typically aware of the sexual signaling; not necessarily nude; common on Instagram and Snapchat.

records.definition: The practice of performing sexual or erotic acts on live webcam streams for a paying online audience.
records.notes: Gerund of 'cam'; implies sex work specifically, not general streaming; a major sector of the digital sex economy; platforms include Chaturbate, MyFreeCams, and OnlyFans Live.

records.definition: Financial domination; a BDSM practice in which the power exchange between dominant and submissive is enacted through monetary tribute, financial control, or enforced poverty.
records.notes: Portmanteau of 'financial' + 'domination'; typically involves a female dominant and male submissive but not exclusively; intersects significantly with sex work, as dominants may treat tribute as income independent of erotic intent.

records.definition: A BDSM dynamic or genre in which a woman takes the dominant role over a submissive partner.
records.notes: Portmanteau of 'female domination'; widely used in online BDSM communities and pornography labeling since the 1990s internet era.

records.definition: A BDSM dynamic or genre in which a man takes the dominant role over a submissive partner.
records.notes: Parallel construction to 'femdom'; less commonly used as a standalone label since male dominance is often treated as the default and therefore less marked in BDSM community vocabulary.

records.definition: The standard clinical Spanish term for the penis, used in medical, educational, and formal contexts across the entire Spanish-speaking world.
Spanish adaptation of Greek/Latin 'phallus'; used in academic, psychoanalytic, literary, and art-historical discourse as a symbol of male sexuality or power beyond mere anatomy.
records.notes: Carries heavy symbolic weight in Lacanian psychoanalysis ('el falo' as the master signifier) and in discussions of phallic imagery in art and architecture; this elevates it above pure anatomy.

records.definition: Lit. 'virile member'; a standard literary and journalistic euphemism for the penis, used when both clinical and crude vocabulary are to be avoided.
records.notes: The preferred periphrasis in Spanish-language newspapers and literary prose. 'Viril' carries connotations of masculine potency that the purely anatomical 'pene' lacks.

records.definition: Lit. 'male genital organ'; a clinical descriptive periphrasis used in formal medical, legal, and sex-education texts when maximum decorum is required.
records.notes: Typically deployed as a noun phrase rather than a lexical item; more common in legal documents, clinical reports, and formal sex-ed materials than in speech.

records.definition: The glans penis: the cone-shaped distal head of the penis and the most densely innervated part of the external male genitalia.
records.notes: Masculine noun in Spanish (el glande). Known to most educated adults but rarely used in casual speech; recognition drops among those with minimal formal sex education.

records.definition: The retractable fold of skin covering the glans penis in uncircumcised males; the foreskin.
records.notes: Recognition is somewhat lower than other anatomical terms because circumcision is uncommon in Latin America and Spain, making the concept familiar but the clinical term less frequently invoked in practice.

records.definition: The urethra: the duct carrying urine from the bladder and, in males, semen during ejaculation; the central conduit of the penis.
records.notes: Applies anatomically to both sexes; listed here because it is the primary internal channel of the male organ. Widely taught in school biology curricula.

records.definition: Corpus cavernosum: one of the paired columns of erectile tissue in the penis that engorge with blood to produce erection.
records.notes: Highly specialized anatomical term; recognized mainly by healthcare professionals, medical students, and the well-educated. Below-average recognition reflects the term's absence from standard school curricula.

records.definition: The dominant crude Spain-Spanish slang for the penis; equivalent in frequency and register to English 'cock'.
records.notes: Absolutely central to Spanish (Spain) vulgar vocabulary and well-known across Latin America via media. 'Una polla' also means 'a hen' (poultry), which produces constant comic ambiguity. Common in expletives: '¡una polla!', 'me importa una polla'.

records.definition: The dominant crude Latin American slang for the penis; also one of the most versatile expletive intensifiers in Mexican and Central American Spanish.
records.notes: Literally 'yardarm' (nautical spar). Extremely productive in fixed expressions: '¡qué verga!' (exclamation of frustration/surprise), 'vale verga' (it's worthless), 'a toda verga' (at full speed). Possibly the highest-frequency vulgar noun in Mexican Spanish.

records.definition: Crude Spain-Spanish slang for the penis, strongest in Andalusia, Extremadura, and Castile.
records.notes: Less widespread in Spain's north; used in dismissive phrases like 'en la picha' (in the dick = nowhere, dismissal). Some use also documented in parts of the Southern Cone via migration but primarily Iberian.

records.definition: Mild, often childlike slang for the penis; literally 'whistle' or 'horn'; used across the entire Spanish-speaking world.
records.notes: One of the most universally recognized penis slang terms in Spanish, often used with young children or in humorous contexts. Central to the fixed expression 'no me importa un pito' (I couldn't care less), where the trivializing sense of 'whistle' carries the semantic weight.

records.definition: Crude slang for the penis; literally 'tail'; predominantly used in Spain.
records.notes: Shares the 'tail' metaphor with several other languages. The idiom 'irse con el rabo entre las piernas' (to leave with one's tail between one's legs) deliberately exploits the double meaning for added humiliation.

records.definition: Crude slang for the penis; literally 'turnip'; used primarily in Spain as a humorous or mildly derogatory term.
records.notes: The vegetable homonym makes double entendres unavoidable whenever turnips appear in conversation or on menus. Also used as a mild insult for a stupid person, mirroring English 'dick' used as an insult.

records.definition: Crude regional slang for the penis; used in southern and central Spain and independently in Central America (Honduras, Nicaragua).
records.notes: In Spain also means 'stupid person' or 'idiot' as a secondary meaning. In Central America the sexual meaning is primary. Etymology is disputed — possibly from Basque or Arabic substrate. Its dual distribution across Spain and Central America reflects independent parallel development.

records.definition: Extremely crude River Plate (Argentina/Uruguay) slang for the penis; among the most vulgar penis terms in Rioplatense Spanish.
records.notes: So strongly associated with the River Plate that other Spanish speakers immediately tag it as Argentinian or Uruguayan. 'Una poronga' used as a dismissal means 'absolutely nothing'. Widely known outside the region through Argentine film and television.

records.definition: Very crude River Plate (Argentina/Uruguay) slang for the penis; also used as a general expletive and intensifier.
records.notes: Uniquely in Argentine Spanish, 'pija' has a second entirely unrelated meaning: 'posh' or 'preppy' (describing upper-class affectation). This creates sharp contextual ambiguity and frequent humor specific to Rioplatense. The duality is not present in Uruguayan usage.

records.definition: Very crude slang for the penis; dominant in Caribbean Spanish (Cuba, Venezuela, Dominican Republic, Colombia) and widely understood across Latin America.
records.notes: Highly productive in fixed expressions: 'no me importa una pinga', 'esto es una pinga' (this is terrible/worthless). Despite phonetic similarity to 'picha', the two terms developed independently and carry distinct regional distributions.

records.definition: Very crude Chilean slang for the penis; also used as a general expletive and dismissive intensifier in Chilean Spanish.
records.notes: Strongly Chilean and largely unknown outside Chile. Produces a sharp semantic collision with the Quechua/Andean Spanish word 'minga' (communal labor), which is entirely unrelated and carries respectful connotations in Andean communities.

records.definition: Crude Mexican slang for the penis; in the same dialect also slang for the police, derived from Caló.
records.notes: The double meaning (penis/police) creates significant contextual ambiguity in Mexican street speech; the police meaning comes from Romani-influenced Caló. Predominantly Mexico and Central America; less common in South America or Spain.

records.definition: Crude slang for the penis; literally 'bar', 'beam', or 'heavy bolt used to barricade a door'; the metaphor emphasizes size and rigidity.
records.notes: The literal meaning (a thick wooden bar) makes the metaphor self-evident and size-emphasizing. Used in Spain and various Latin American countries. Also used in 'agarrar una tranca' meaning to get very drunk, illustrating how the word operates in multiple unrelated idiomatic domains.

records.definition: Slang for the penis; literally 'bug', 'insect', or 'small creature'; used primarily in Spain.
records.notes: The primary meaning (insect/creature/animal) dominates across Latin America, where the sexual meaning is weak or absent. In Puerto Rico, 'bicho' refers to the vagina rather than the penis, demonstrating a complete regional semantic inversion. Recognition score reflects Spain-primary usage of the sexual meaning.

records.definition: Mild euphemistic slang for the penis; literally 'dove' or 'pigeon'; primarily used in Mexico and Central America, often in speech directed at children.
records.notes: Considered childlike and unthreatening; the dove metaphor appears across Romance-language traditions. In Mexico also used in the expression 'sacar la paloma' (to take out the dove = to expose the penis). Recognized broadly because the term 'paloma' is ubiquitous, but the sexual meaning is strongest in the Mexican register.

records.definition: Crude slang for the penis; literally 'club', 'cudgel', or 'garrote'; the metaphor emphasizes blunt size and force.
records.notes: The primary meanings (a heavy wooden stick and Spain's traditional method of capital punishment by strangulation) give the metaphor both a size implication and an inadvertently sinister connotation. Less frequent than 'polla' but widely understood in Spain.

records.definition: Mild diminutive slang for the penis; the '-ín' suffix (of Asturian-Leonese origin) imparts a childlike or affectionate tone; used primarily in northern and central Spain.
records.notes: The diminutive register makes this functionally equivalent to English 'willy' or 'winkle' — inoffensive enough for parental use. Often deployed humorously by adults to deflate sexual tension. The '-ín' suffix is a northern Iberian diminutive variant, distinguishing this from the more widespread '-ito' form.

records.definition: Crude slang for the penis, dominant in Chilean vernacular and common across Peru, Bolivia, and parts of Central America.
records.notes: The default crude penis word in Chile; also used in Peru and Bolivia; less common in Mexico and largely unknown in Spain.

records.definition: Rioplatense slang for the penis.
records.notes: Primarily Argentina and Uruguay; 'Pirulo' is also the brand name of a popular ice cream bar in the region, generating persistent double entendres.

records.definition: Iberian Spanish slang for the penis, derived from the black poplar tree (chopo), whose tall, columnar form evokes a phallus.
records.notes: Primarily Spain; the black poplar is known for its straight, upright growth habit; limited penetration in Latin America.

records.definition: Slang for the penis using the word for 'log' or 'trunk,' implying substantial size and rigidity.
records.notes: Used across Spain and Latin America; implies a thick or large member; 'tronco' also means 'mate/buddy' in colloquial Spanish, occasionally producing ambiguity.

records.definition: Slang for the penis derived from 'mallet' or 'sledgehammer,' emphasizing forceful size.
records.notes: Primarily Iberian Spanish; the mallet metaphor foregrounds force and heft rather than length; less common than tronco across Latin America.

records.definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'walking stick' or 'cane,' playing on upright phallic shape.
records.notes: A mild, humorous metaphor used across Spanish-speaking regions; lower vulgarity than direct penis slang.

records.definition: English loanword adopted into Spanish as humorous slang for the penis, referencing the handheld video-game controller.
records.notes: Peak usage late 1990s–early 2000s, aligned with the rise of home gaming; still recognized but less actively used; same metaphor exists in English.

records.definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'cucumber,' a widespread vegetable-shape metaphor.
records.notes: One of the most widespread penis euphemisms in Spanish; the cucumber metaphor appears across many languages; 'no importar un pepino' (not to care a cucumber) adds ironic layering in Spain.

records.definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'carrot,' referencing its elongated tapered shape.
records.notes: More playful than crude; less common than pepino as a penis metaphor in Spanish; the carrot's color and taper evoke the circumcised glans.

records.definition: Slang for the penis using the word for 'bone,' playing on both structural hardness and the English cognate 'boner' for erection.
records.notes: The bone-erection metaphor works cross-linguistically; can specifically connote erection rather than the flaccid organ; used across Latin America and Spain.

records.definition: Euphemistic slang for the penis using the word for 'tool,' one of the most universal phallic metaphors across human languages.
records.notes: Maps directly to the English slang 'tool'; among the mildest and most socially acceptable penis euphemisms in Spanish; widely used in humorous contexts.

records.definition: Mild euphemism for the penis using the word for 'apparatus' or 'device,' used in quasi-clinical and humorous registers.
records.notes: One of the most demure penis references in Spanish; also appears in clinical contexts as 'aparato reproductor' (reproductive system), lending it a veneer of respectability even in crude usage.

records.definition: Mexican slang for the penis derived from 'pirinola,' a traditional wooden spinning top with a tapered, pointed tip.
records.notes: Primarily Mexican Spanish; the pirinola's pointed spinning tip and the act of spinning map onto penetrative connotations; limited recognition outside Mexico.

records.definition: Crude slang for the penis, literally 'beak' or 'tip'; among the most taboo penis terms in Chile, approaching the vulgarity ceiling of Chilean profanity.
records.notes: In Chile, 'pico' rivals 'pichula' in vulgarity and is censored on broadcast television; also used in Colombia and Peru; 'al pico' functions as a strong dismissive expletive in Chilean Spanish.

records.definition: Mexican and Central American slang for the penis, sometimes carrying connotations of thickness or large size.
records.notes: Primarily Mexico and Central America; in non-sexual registers 'choncho' can mean 'fat' or 'chubby,' which transfers into the size implication in sexual use.

records.definition: Rioplatense slang for the penis; literally 'Turk,' likely originating from ethnic stereotypes about Levantine immigrants in Argentina.
records.notes: Primarily Argentina; Argentina received substantial Levantine Arab immigration in the 19th–20th centuries, colloquially called 'turcos'; the ethnic attribution of sexual prowess to this group appears to underlie the slang.

records.definition: Rioplatense slang for the penis; literally a squat clay jug or earthenware pot, metaphorically referencing genital shape.
records.notes: Primarily Argentina and Uruguay; in Uruguay 'botija' separately means 'kid' or 'boy' in everyday slang, adding double-meaning potential; low recognition outside the River Plate region.

records.definition: Augmentative of 'polla' (the dominant Iberian Spanish crude term for penis), meaning a large penis; the '-ón' suffix marks exceptional size.
records.notes: Derived from 'polla' + augmentative '-ón'; primarily Iberian Spanish where 'polla' is the default vulgar penis word; register and tone parallel English 'big dick.'

records.definition: Spanish slang for the glans penis; literally 'cocoon' or 'flower bud,' evoking the rounded tip of the penis; simultaneously a high-frequency general insult in Spain.
records.notes: Has dual currency in Spain: anatomically specific (glans) and as a general-purpose insult roughly equivalent to British 'bellend' or 'knob'; both meanings are simultaneously active; less common in Latin America.

records.definition: The clinical term for the internal muscular canal extending from the cervix to the vulvar vestibule; the standard anatomical term in Spanish medical and educational contexts.
records.notes: Identical spelling to the English clinical term; Latin origin; frequently misapplied by lay speakers to denote the external genitalia (vulva) as well.

records.definition: The clinical term for the external female genitalia, encompassing the labia majora and minora, clitoris, and vaginal opening.
records.notes: Identical to the English clinical term; significantly underrecognized by the general population relative to 'vagina,' despite being the visible external anatomy; recognition has risen with sex-education campaigns.

records.definition: The clinical Spanish term for the vaginal lips (labia), used generically to cover both the labia majora and labia minora.
records.notes: Generic clinical term; the more precise distinction is 'labios mayores' (labia majora) and 'labios menores' (labia minora); 'labios vaginales' is preferred in sex-education contexts for accessibility.

records.definition: The clinical Spanish term for the vaginal introitus — the external entrance to the vaginal canal.
records.notes: Highly specialized medical terminology; rarely encountered outside gynecological or anatomical discourse; the full form 'introito vaginal' is more common in clinical writing than the standalone noun.

records.definition: The clinical and literary Spanish term for the mons pubis — the rounded fatty prominence over the pubic symphysis; literally 'Mount of Venus.'
records.notes: Translates Latin 'mons Veneris'; bridges clinical anatomy and literary tradition via the mythological reference to Venus; known to educated speakers but not universally recognized.

records.definition: The clinical Spanish term specifically denoting the internal muscular channel of the vagina from the cervix to the vaginal opening.
records.notes: More anatomically precise than 'vagina' alone, emphasizing the tubular structure; common in obstetric contexts (e.g., 'parto por canal vaginal' = vaginal delivery).

records.definition: The most widespread and forceful crude Spanish slang for the vagina; also functions as a standalone expletive analogous to English 'fuck' or 'shit'.
records.notes: In Spain the expletive use (¡coño!) is so pervasive that the anatomical force is often weakened; in Latin America the anatomical reference remains more foregrounded and carries stronger shock value.

records.definition: Crude Spanish slang for the vagina, primarily used in Spain.
records.notes: In Spain 'chocho' also informally means a sentimental or doting person (from 'chochear,' to become senile with affection); the sexual meaning predominates in sexual contexts but the dual use is common.

records.definition: Highly offensive Rioplatense slang for the vagina; in all other Spanish dialects the word innocuously means 'shell' (seashell, mollusc shell).
records.notes: The sexual meaning is essentially exclusive to Argentina and Uruguay; everywhere else 'concha' is a neutral everyday word. This creates persistent miscommunication and dark comedy when Rioplatense speakers use the word abroad.

records.definition: Crude slang for the vagina literally meaning 'crack,' 'split,' or 'slit,' used across the Spanish-speaking world.
records.notes: The dual meaning (crack/split in general usage; vagina in sexual slang) is context-dependent and understood pan-regionally. One of the more anatomically descriptive metaphors in this list.

records.definition: Dialectal Spanish slang for the vagina, primarily used in eastern and southern Spain (Valencia, Catalonia, Aragon regions).
records.notes: A relatively regional term with limited penetration outside Spain. May derive from a crevice-related etymological root. Low recognition in Latin America.

records.definition: In Cuba and parts of the Caribbean, slang for the vagina derived from the tropical fruit of the same name; elsewhere in the Spanish-speaking world the word refers only to the fruit.
records.notes: The sexual meaning is so dominant in Cuba that Cubans typically substitute 'fruta bomba' when referring to the papaya fruit to avoid the double entendre. In Mexico, Spain, and most of Latin America the word is entirely innocent.

records.definition: Mexican crude slang for the vagina; the word also refers to a type of unrefined brown-sugar sweet or a bundle of dried grain husks in non-sexual contexts.
records.notes: The innocent meanings (brown-sugar candy, cornhusk bundle) coexist with the crude slang in Mexico, producing constant double entendres. Also used in parts of Central America in the sexual sense.

records.definition: Crude slang for the vagina used primarily in Venezuela, Colombia, and parts of the Caribbean.
records.notes: Also used informally in some Venezuelan and Colombian families as a children's word for the vagina, which reduces its shock value relative to other terms. Augmentative 'totona' is also attested.

records.definition: Crude Spanish slang for the vagina; the standard meaning of the word is a soft bread roll or bun.
records.notes: The baked-goods metaphor is widespread in Spain; the sexual meaning also exists in Cuba and parts of Latin America. The dual use generates food-related double entendres in Spanish speech.

records.definition: Crude Andalusian and southern Spanish slang for the vagina, with limited distribution outside that region.
records.notes: Primarily a term from Andalusia and Extremadura in southern Spain. Virtually unknown in Latin America. Etymology uncertain.

records.definition: Slang for the vagina derived from the word for clam, referencing the bivalve's shape; used across Spain and much of Latin America.
records.notes: The food metaphor (clam/bivalve) gives this slightly softer connotations than terms like 'coño,' though it is still distinctly crude. Widely understood pan-regionally.

records.definition: Caribbean and Central American slang for the vagina; in Mexico the same word (typically plural 'chichis') primarily refers to breasts instead.
records.notes: Significant regional semantic divergence: Mexican 'chichis' = breasts; Cuban and Central American 'chichi' = vagina. Derived from babytalk reduplication. Moderate crude score reflects the infantilizing diminutive form.

records.definition: A pan-regional Spanish euphemism for the vagina meaning 'cave,' understood across the Spanish-speaking world.
records.notes: The cave metaphor is transparent and widely understood; its euphemistic register makes it substantially less offensive than direct anatomical slang. Appears frequently in ribald humor and double-entendre wordplay.

records.definition: Cuban and Central American slang for the vagina; in other Spanish dialects the word refers to a tobacco pipe or, in some regions, a well or water source.
records.notes: The innocent meanings (tobacco pipe, water source) coexist with the sexual slang in different regions. The sexual meaning is primary in Cuba and parts of Central America. Also used in some Colombian dialects.

records.definition: A mild Spanish slang term for the vagina derived from 'minino' (a small cat or kitten), directly parallel to English 'pussy' in its kitten-derived etymology.
records.notes: The closest structural equivalent to English 'pussy' in Spanish — same animal, same metaphorical extension, similar register. Mild enough to appear in mainstream Spanish media. More common in Spain than Latin America.

records.definition: A widespread crude slang term for the vagina used across Spain and Latin America.
records.notes: Also a common Spanish nickname (short for various names). In some Colombian and Venezuelan regions 'cuca' refers to a type of insect or beetle. The sexual meaning is well-established across most dialects.

records.definition: Colombian crude slang for the vagina; in standard Spanish the word means the seed, pit, or stone of a fruit.
records.notes: The sexual meaning is specific to Colombia and nearby Andean regions; elsewhere 'pepa' simply means a fruit seed or, in some Latin American drug slang, a pill. Also a nickname for women named Josefa.

records.definition: Crude slang for the vagina distributed across Spain and Latin America; a feminine-form variant related to the Iberian Spanish term 'chocho.'
records.notes: More broadly distributed than 'chocho,' which skews Iberian. In some contexts 'chocha' also serves as an archaic adjective meaning 'senile' or 'doting' (same root as 'chochear'). Also the name of the Eurasian woodcock bird (Scolopax rusticola).

records.definition: A Spanish euphemistic slang for the vagina derived from 'cotorra' (a small parrot or parakeet), primarily used in Spain.
records.notes: The sexual meaning is substantially less common than the bird meaning; the word's primary everyday sense is a noisy or chatty person. The vaginal usage is largely Spanish-peninsula-specific with low recognition in Latin America.

records.definition: A euphemistic literary slang for the vagina meaning 'grotto' or 'cave,' used informally and in sexual humor across the Spanish-speaking world.
records.notes: One of the softest terms in this list; the primary meaning (natural cave or ornamental garden grotto) vastly predominates. The sexual connotation surfaces mainly in ribald wordplay and erotica rather than casual everyday slang.

records.definition: A very mild euphemism for the vagina meaning 'little thing,' used pan-regionally in child-directed speech and in adult contexts requiring coy indirection.
records.notes: Standard in childrearing across the Spanish-speaking world to name genitalia without explicit language. Among adults signals deliberate coyness or embarrassment. The diminutive suffix '-ita' is doing significant register-softening work.

records.definition: Dominican Republic and broader Caribbean slang for the vagina, derived from the word for sponge cake or biscuit.
records.notes: The pastry double entendre is characteristic of Caribbean Spanish ribald humor. Also used in Puerto Rico with the same sexual meaning. In Spain and most of Latin America 'bizcocho' refers only to the baked good.

records.definition: A Chilean compound expletive literally meaning 'your mother's cunt,' functioning as a general-purpose intensifier and insult of maximum severity; the most powerful swearword in Chilean Spanish.
records.notes: Etymologically derived from the vagina slang 'concha' (Rioplatense/Chilean) combined with 'su madre' (your mother), but the compound functions as a general expletive analogous to English 'motherfucker' rather than as an anatomical reference. Also written 'conchetumadre' in informal orthography. Recognized pan-regionally through Chilean cultural reach.

records.definition: A low-frequency dialectal Spanish slang term for the vagina with very limited regional distribution.
records.notes: Among the rarest terms in this list; appears in limited Spanish regional dialects and has minimal documentation. May be hyperlocal or generational. Low inter-regional recognition even within Spain.

records.definition: Venezuelan and Caribbean slang for the vagina; in standard Spanish the word 'bobo/boba' is the common adjective meaning 'silly,' 'dumb,' or 'foolish.'
records.notes: The sexual meaning is strongly regional (Venezuela, parts of the Caribbean coast); Spanish speakers outside that region typically know the word only as the adjective meaning 'stupid' or 'silly,' creating potential for confusion or double entendre.

records.definition: Slang term for the vagina used primarily in Venezuelan and some Colombian Spanish.
records.notes: Predominantly Caribbean/northern South American usage; rare in Spain or the Southern Cone.

records.definition: Poetic euphemism for the vagina using the word for 'flower' to evoke femininity and delicacy.
records.notes: Used in romantic, literary, or coy registers; not clinical but not crude. The English 'flower' is deployed as an identical euphemism.

records.definition: Childish diminutive euphemism for the vagina used in baby talk or to soften the anatomical reference.
records.notes: The '-ita' diminutive softens it considerably; primarily deployed when speaking to or about young children regarding anatomy. Geographic distribution is uneven.

records.definition: Standard formal and semi-clinical Spanish term for the female breasts.
records.notes: Default elevated-register word; used in medical, journalistic, and polite social contexts. Less technical than 'glándulas mamarias' but more formal than 'pechos'.

records.definition: Formal term for breasts, cognate with English 'mammary'; used in medical and anatomical contexts.
records.notes: 'Mamas' also means 'mothers/mamas,' requiring context to disambiguate the anatomical sense.

records.definition: Fully clinical anatomical term for the mammary glands, used in medical and scientific contexts.
records.notes: Strictly technical; effectively never used in everyday speech. Direct cognate with English 'mammary glands'.

records.definition: The pigmented circular area of skin surrounding the nipple; the same term in Spanish and English.
records.notes: International anatomical term identical in form and meaning to the English. Recognized mainly by those with some medical or sex-education exposure.

records.definition: The most widely used crude slang term for female breasts across the entire Spanish-speaking world.
records.notes: Universal across all Spanish dialects; the default vulgar word for breasts. Cognate with Italian 'tette' and Portuguese 'tetas'; etymology from Latin 'tetta'.

records.definition: Common mild-register term for female breasts, literally 'chests'; acceptable in most social contexts.
records.notes: Occupies the middle ground between clinical ('senos') and crude ('tetas'); used freely in mainstream media and advertising without being vulgar. Anatomically sex-neutral but culturally applied primarily to female breasts.

records.definition: Cute, childish slang for breasts, predominantly used in Mexican Spanish.
records.notes: Strong association with Mexican vernacular; the register mirrors English 'boobies' almost exactly. Familiar to non-Mexican speakers through media but not natively used outside Mexico.

records.definition: Slang term for breasts common in Mexican and Central American Spanish, slightly more crude than 'bubis'.
records.notes: Very common in Mexican vernacular and Central America; recognized but not natively used in Spain or South America. Possibly reduplicative baby-talk origin.

records.definition: Colloquial slang for breasts used in Colombian and some other South American varieties of Spanish.
records.notes: Named after the common given name Lola; the playful personification via a woman's name is a recurring pattern in Spanish breast slang. Limited geographic spread.

records.definition: Crude slang for large female breasts, comparing them to melons; implies impressive size.
records.notes: The English 'melons' and Spanish 'melones' are cognate slang with identical meaning, connotations, and implied size praise; understood across all dialects.

records.definition: Very crude slang for breasts borrowed from the word for animal udders; derogatory and dehumanizing.
records.notes: One of the most demeaning terms for breasts in Spanish, directly comparing a woman's body to livestock anatomy. English 'udders' carries the identical dehumanizing charge.

records.definition: Slang for female breasts used in parts of Spain and Latin America; etymology likely from the feminine given name Dominga.
records.notes: Personification via a woman's given name follows a common Spanish pattern (cf. 'lolas', 'nenas'). Moderately crude; not universal across all regions.

records.definition: Humorous-crude slang for female breasts derived from 'chicken breast'; implies fleshy volume.
records.notes: Primary meaning is the cut of poultry meat; its application to human breasts is comedic and mildly crude. The humor comes from the shared shape and texture association.

records.definition: Diminutive of 'tetas'; refers to small breasts or is used affectionately to reduce the bluntness of the base term.
records.notes: The '-itas' diminutive softens 'tetas' slightly but it remains crude. Can imply small size or serve as an affectionate register shift; mirrors English 'titties' closely.

records.definition: Poetic-humorous euphemism for small, perky breasts; literally 'little doves' or 'popcorn'.
records.notes: The image is of small, rounded, uplifted forms — either doves or popcorn kernels. Playful and non-offensive; less widely distributed than mainstream slang terms.

records.definition: Playful slang for breasts using the word for 'little girls/babies'; personifies them as a pair.
records.notes: Mirrors the English euphemism 'the girls' for breasts — personifying them as a pair of feminine companions. Regional spread uneven; more common in informal online contexts.

records.definition: Regional slang for female breasts in some Latin American varieties of Spanish.
records.notes: The primary meaning of 'chola' is an Andean indigenous or mestiza woman (Andean Spanish) or a Chicana gang-affiliated woman (US/MX Spanish), both carrying strong ethnic identity weight; use as breast slang is geographically restricted and risks conflation with those ethnic terms.

records.definition: Crude slang for breasts using the word for 'balls/spheres'; less common in this sense than its primary use for testicles.
records.notes: 'Pelotas' primarily means testicles across most dialects (Argentina, Spain); its application to breasts is context-dependent and requires speaker-gender and conversational framing to disambiguate. Listed under breasts per section context.

records.definition: The standard clinical and formal term for the testicles in Spanish.
records.notes: Direct cognate with English 'testicles'; used in medical, educational, and formal journalistic contexts. Not inherently vulgar but sounds clinical and stiff in casual speech.

records.definition: Clinical anatomical term for the gonads (testicles or ovaries), used exclusively in medical and scientific contexts.
records.notes: Direct cognate with English 'gonads'; sex-neutral term referring to either male or female reproductive glands. Essentially never used in casual speech.

records.definition: The clinical and anatomical term for the scrotum, the skin pouch enclosing the testicles.
records.notes: Direct cognate with English 'scrotum'; used in medical contexts. More widely recognized than 'gónadas' due to sex-education exposure but still uncommon in casual speech.

records.definition: Extremely widespread crude slang for testicles, literally 'eggs'; also used metaphorically for courage or audacity.
records.notes: One of the most universal Spanish slang terms, understood across all dialects. Primary literal meaning is 'eggs' (food), creating perpetual double-entendre potential; metaphorical extension to courage mirrors English 'balls' precisely.

records.definition: Very common crude slang for testicles; also widely used metaphorically to mean courage or audacity.
records.notes: Borrowed into English as a mild intensifier meaning nerve or guts; one of the most internationally recognized Spanish words.

records.definition: Common slang for testicles; literally 'balls' as in sports balls; also used to mean nerve or audacity.

records.definition: Slang for testicles; literally 'balls'; widely used across multiple Spanish-speaking regions.
Crude Mexican slang for testicles; emphatic orthographic variant of huevos (eggs); signals maximally vulgar register.

records.definition: Regional Iberian Spanish slang for testicles; also the dialectal word for truffles (the fungus) in some areas.

records.definition: Mexican slang for testicles, derived from the Nahuatl word tanatli; also used colloquially to mean personal belongings or stuff.

records.definition: Humorous crude slang for testicles; literally 'meatballs,' evoking shape similarity.

records.definition: Playful, somewhat old-fashioned euphemism for testicles used in Spain; not aggressive in register.
records.notes: Considered quaint or humorous rather than transgressive; less commonly used by younger Spanish speakers; no clear etymology.

records.definition: Slang for testicles; literally 'coconuts,' evoking shape and paired nature; mildly crude.

records.definition: Slang for testicles; literally 'walnuts' or 'nuts'; food metaphor parallel to English 'nuts.'

records.definition: Euphemistic slang for testicles; literally 'companions' or 'buddies,' referring to their paired anatomy.
records.notes: Mildest possible register for this anatomy; personification humor rather than crude intent.

records.definition: Crude slang for testicles; literally 'hanging bits' or 'dangling things,' emphasizing ptosis and pendulousness.
records.notes: More unflattering in tone than cojones; implies a sagging or flaccid quality; can also refer to other hanging flesh generically.

records.definition: Clinical anatomical term for the anus; the external opening of the rectum.

records.definition: Clinical anatomical term for the anal sphincter, the ring of muscle controlling the aperture of the anus.
Very common crude term for the anus or buttocks; the most universally recognized Spanish expletive for this anatomy.

records.definition: Crude slang for the anus; literally 'little eyelet' from ojo (eye); also a strong insult for a contemptible or selfish person.

records.definition: Mexican and Central American slang for the anus or buttocks; derived from fondo (bottom/base).

records.definition: Rioplatense crude slang for the anus; etymology debated — possibly vesre (Argentine backslang) of roto or from Italian dialectal roots.

records.definition: Slang for the anus or buttocks; literally 'old junk' or 'rubbish piece'; also the standard word for a guitar fret.

records.definition: Crude slang for the anus; literally 'hole'; the everyday word applied to the anal opening in sexual or crude speech.

records.definition: Crude slang for the anus; literally 'pit' or 'hollow'; also used loosely for any penetrable orifice in sexual speech.

records.definition: Chilean coded slang for the anus; the numeral seven, whose written shape evokes a seated figure with the anal region exposed.
