records.notes: Loanword from Polish/Ukrainian; the foreign phonology can intensify its offensive edge in Russian; widely understood and used in Russian criminal speech.

records.definition: A vile, morally depraved, or nasty person; in criminal argot directed at women, implies sexual and moral corruption combined.
records.notes: Less specifically sexual than шалава; the sexual insult dimension emerges primarily from gendered application and context; also used for treacherous male figures.

records.definition: Literally 'hide/pelt/skin'; criminal argot for a sexually available woman or prostitute who sells herself.
records.notes: Dual meaning in феня: prostitute or sexually available woman AND informer/snitch — context determines which reading applies; both usages frame the person as something disposable.

records.definition: A girl or young woman (crude); literally 'heifer' (young female bovine); objectifying and mildly contemptuous but extremely widespread.
records.notes: Simplified spelling of тёлка (without ё); occupies a register similar to English 'chick' or British 'bird'; crude but not maximally offensive — also appears as entries 8 and 12 in this dataset.

records.definition: A girl or young woman (crude); literally 'heifer'; objectifying and mildly contemptuous but pervasive in colloquial Russian.
records.notes: Standard orthographic form (with ё); one of the most common crude-colloquial terms for a young woman in Russian; also appears as entries 7 and 12 in this dataset (simplified and repeated forms).

records.definition: Literally 'washcloth or bath loofah'; prison and criminal argot for a woman regarded purely as a sexual use-object to be worn down through repeated use.
records.notes: The washcloth metaphor is specifically apt: something used over and over until it deteriorates; more confined to criminal and prison environments than the other objectifying terms in this section.

records.definition: A woman who puts out readily; derived from давать (to give), the sexual idiom meaning to be sexually available; implies a promiscuous woman who never refuses.
records.notes: Transparent derivation from давать ('to give/put out'); the -алка suffix is an agent-noun suffix turning the verb into 'the one who gives (sex)'; always pejorative.

records.definition: Literally 'floor litter, bedding, or mat'; criminal argot for a woman who is laid down on by anyone — the image of a sexual doormat.
records.notes: Evokes something placed on the floor for anyone to walk on or lie upon; harsher and more specifically dehumanizing than тёлка in its denotative imagery.

records.definition: A girl or young woman (crude); literally 'heifer'; objectifying and mildly contemptuous. Duplicate entry — see entries 7 and 8.
records.notes: Third occurrence of this word in the source dataset; entries 7, 8, and 12 are all the same word in differing orthographic conventions (е vs. ё) or as a repeated item.

records.definition: Literally 'meat or flesh'; criminal argot that reduces women to raw sexual matter, the most extreme level of dehumanizing objectification.
records.notes: мясо also circulates in gaming and internet contexts ('пушечное мясо' = cannon fodder), reinforcing its sense of disposable material; in the sexual context the reduction is total.

records.definition: Literally 'frame/shot/cadre/personnel file'; criminal argot for a person — typically female — identified and marked as a candidate for sexual exploitation.
records.notes: In general Russian slang кадр means 'what a character/specimen'; the criminal-argot overlay frames the person as a personnel file to be acted upon — selected, assessed, and used.

records.definition: Sexual abuse perpetrated within the дедовщина system — the institutionalized caste-based hazing hierarchy of the Soviet and Russian military — by senior conscripts against junior ones.
records.notes: Дедовщина (from дед, 'grandfather/old timer') is a Soviet and post-Soviet military institution in which senior conscripts systematically abuse juniors across a rigid caste ladder; the sexual component uses rape and coercion to establish dominance and silence reporting through homophobic shame. No English term captures both the institutional caste structure and the sexual violence dimension simultaneously.

records.definition: Plural of дух ('spirit/ghost'); the lowest caste in the дедовщина military hierarchy — first-year conscripts subjected to labor, humiliation, and sexual abuse by senior soldiers.
records.notes: Also used as a term for enemy fighters (Afghan mujahideen, Chechen combatants) in military slang. In дедовщина contexts духи are the primary sexual victims. The ghost metaphor implies they are not yet fully real soldiers — and therefore not entitled to human dignity.

records.definition: Singular of духи; a single first-year conscript at the bottom of the дедовщина caste hierarchy, subject to sexual abuse and forced servitude by senior soldiers.
records.notes: Singular form of entry 16. Primary civilian meanings are 'spirit/soul' and 'scent/aroma'; the military hazing meaning is entirely register-specific.

records.definition: A raw, inexperienced military recruit or sailor; in дедовщина contexts, a novice conscript at or near the bottom of the hazing caste and therefore exposed to sexual and physical abuse.
records.notes: Originally navy slang — likely from a small worthless fish; migrated across all service branches. Functions more as a general insult for inexperience than a formally fixed caste rank in the way дух/духи is; overlap with that concept is strong.

records.definition: Literally 'young one'; in the дедовщина hierarchy, the second-year conscript rank — above духи but still subordinate to деды — both victim and perpetrator in the cycle of sexual hazing.
records.notes: The intermediate caste: молодые have survived their first year and are now entitled to victimize духи while remaining subject to the деды. This structural position perpetuates the cycle. No English concept captures the intermediate perpetrator-victim role in a military sexual-hazing caste hierarchy.

records.definition: To force or coerce; in дедовщина and criminal argot contexts, a euphemistic verb for compelling someone to perform a sexual act — i.e., rape or sexual coercion.
records.notes: The verb itself is neutral (to compel/force); the sexual meaning is entirely context-dependent. Used in дедовщина discourse as a distancing or legalistic euphemism for rape.

records.definition: Literally 'to lower or put down'; in Russian prison and criminal culture, to forcibly rape a man — typically anally — in order to permanently demote him to the опущенные caste, the irreversibly degraded stratum of the criminal hierarchy.
records.notes: One of the most culturally loaded concepts in Russian criminal culture. The act creates a permanent and irreversible caste change: the victim becomes опущенный ('lowered/degraded'), permanently untouchable and barred from normal social contact with other prisoners. No English concept captures both the specific act and the permanent social-caste consequence. The matching dедовщина usage transfers this prison logic into the military barracks context.

records.definition: A descriptive or meta phrase for homophobic slurs used in дедовщина contexts to shame sexually abused junior soldiers and prevent them from reporting abuse.
records.notes: A category label rather than a single slur; included in дедовщина sexual-hazing vocabulary because homophobic shaming is the primary silencing mechanism — perpetrators frame rape as making the victim gay, ensuring victims cannot report without identifying themselves as homosexual under Russia's hostile social and legal climate.

records.definition: One of the most powerful Russian mat phrases; literally '(I/he) fucked your mother'; deployed as an expression of extreme rage, contempt, or emphasis.
records.notes: Structurally parallel to English 'motherfucker' but second-person accusative ('your mother') rather than a compound noun. Part of core Russian мат — the highly restricted obscene register. Extremely pervasive in military speech; saying it to a superior can result in serious consequences; its frequency in barracks environments is near-constant.

records.definition: To curse at or verbally abuse someone using мат — the Russian system of strongly obscene language — as a form of aggression, dominance, or humiliation.
records.notes: Мат is a discrete register of Russian built around a small set of root words (хуй, пизда, ёб/ебать, блядь, etc.) with specific social rules governing permissible contexts. Материть is the transitive form — to direct мат AT a person rather than merely using profanity in general. Pervasive in дедовщина as an ongoing instrument of dominance; no English verb captures both the specific register system and the directional-abuse function.

records.definition: To deceive someone by creating a false online identity for romantic or sexual purposes.
records.notes: English term used directly in Tagalog; common in Filipino online dating and social media discussions.

records.definition: Fake/private Instagram account used for sharing intimate, sexual, or niche content away from main profile.
records.notes: Fake + Instagram; used in Filipino online sexual content discourse; less common than OF (OnlyFans).

records.definition: Secondary private social media account used for sharing explicit or intimate content not appropriate for one's main account.
records.notes: Filipino internet usage diverges from English; 'spam account' in PH context often means private intimate content account.

records.definition: OnlyFans; used as noun (have an OF) and verb (OF-ing) for the subscription-based adult content platform.
records.notes: English abbreviation used directly; rapid adoption in Philippine online sex work discourse since 2020.

records.definition: Euphemism for sexual material produced for online platforms; 'making content' = producing explicit material.
records.notes: English word used as euphemism; 'magcontent' (to make content) is a Filipino term for producing sexual media.

records.definition: Secret (romantic or sexual) partner; someone kept hidden from one's main relationship or family.
records.notes: From Spanish 'secreto'; common in Philippine social media discourse about hidden relationships.

records.definition: A style of flamboyant gay expression combining bakla camp with jejemon/texting subculture aesthetics; a specific subcultural identity.
records.notes: Novel concept: intersection of bakla camp and Filipino jejetext culture; bekimon = beki + jejemon; peak ~2010-2015.

records.definition: The distinctive cant or secret language of Filipino bakla/gay community; a sociolect mixing Tagalog, English, and creative wordplay.
records.notes: Novel concept: Philippines-specific sociolect with extensive vocabulary; includes reversed words, word play, and English borrowings.

records.definition: Filipino gay vernacular; the broader term for the language variety used by bakla/gay community in the Philippines.
records.notes: Novel concept: encompasses swardspeak and other bakla linguistic innovations; widely known and partially adopted by mainstream.

records.definition: A niche subculture combining jejetext (Filipino texting slang) with bekimon/bakla culture; characterized by elaborate text styling.
records.notes: Novel concept: very specific Filipino internet subculture; jejebeki combines jeje (texting style) + beki (gay slang).

records.definition: The spoken gay vernacular of the Filipino bakla community; the oral/performative dimension of swardspeak.
records.notes: Partial overlap with swardspeak; 'gay speak' emphasizes verbal performance aspect; widely recognized.

records.definition: Best friend; gay lingo term of affection for one's closest friend; from English 'best friend' in bakla pronunciation.
records.notes: Novel concept only as gay lingo term; the word itself means 'best friend' but the form is specifically bakla/swardspeak.

records.definition: Short form of 'bespren' or 'beshie'; bakla term of address for a close friend; now widely adopted in mainstream Filipino youth speech.
records.notes: Crossed over from gay lingo to mainstream; now used by non-gay Filipinos; originated in bakla community.

records.definition: Gossip, news, or intimate conversation; central to bakla social bonding; 'mag-chika' = to gossip/chat.
records.notes: Novel concept: originated in gay community but now universal in Filipino informal speech; the act of chika is a social ritual.

records.definition: 'Just kidding / I was only joking'; bakla word used to retract or soften a statement; from Filipino name 'Charing'.
records.notes: Novel concept: uniquely Filipino gay lingo word for self-deprecating retraction; widely adopted in mainstream.

records.definition: 'Just kidding / never mind'; bakla interjection used to dismiss or walk back a statement; similar to 'charing'.
records.notes: Novel concept: bakla-originated filler word; became mainstream Gen Z Filipino slang; peak ~2012-2018.

records.definition: Aura; the sexual or glamorous presence/magnetism someone projects; in bakla culture, a positive quality of charisma.
records.notes: Novel concept: bakla reinterpretation of 'aura' as performative sexual/glamorous presence; widely adopted.

records.definition: Fabulous, spectacular, extravagant; bakla term for something impressive or over-the-top in a positive sense.
records.notes: Novel concept: central bakla aesthetic term; implies extravagant and sexually confident self-presentation; now mainstream Filipino.

records.definition: Exclamation of shock, excitement, or exaggerated reaction; bakla interjection used for dramatic effect.
records.notes: Novel concept: bakla camp exclamation; onomatopoeic/expressive; used for comic or dramatic emphasis.

records.definition: Unbelievable, outrageous, crazy (in a dramatic sense); bakla/gay term for something shocking or over-the-top.
records.notes: Novel concept: from 'loka' (crazy); bakla intensifier; crossed into mainstream Filipino speech widely.

records.definition: 'Intense / extreme / unbelievable'; in gay community usage often intensified to express sexual excitement or dramatic reaction.
records.notes: From Spanish 'grave'; not exclusively gay lingo but heavily used in bakla camp register with sexual/dramatic inflection.

records.definition: Totally crazy / wild; intensified form of 'loka'; describes outrageous behavior or a wild personality, often affectionately.
records.notes: Novel concept: reduplication of 'loka'; bakla/gay use is affectionate, not pejorative; implies fabulous chaos.

records.definition: The quality or state of being a beshie (best friend); the collective identity of a close gay social circle.
records.notes: Novel concept: English '-ness' suffix added to Filipino 'beshie'; internet-era hybrid word.

records.definition: Sugar / sweetheart; bakla term of endearment for a romantic interest or attractive person.
records.notes: Novel concept: bakla phonetic rendering of 'sugar' with camp affection; used as term of endearment.

records.definition: Ugly or unattractive in a humorous sense; bakla/swardspeak term for someone considered physically undesirable.
records.notes: Novel concept: bakla aesthetic judgment term; used humorously within community; not meant as harsh slur.

records.definition: A man who is the 'kabit' or extramarital lover; a man who maintains an affair with a married or committed person.
records.notes: Novel concept: gendered male form of kabit; the -ero suffix marks male agency; distinct social role in Philippine relationship culture.

records.definition: A woman who is the 'kabit' or extramarital lover; a woman maintained as a secret lover by a married man.
records.notes: Novel concept: explicitly gendered female form of kabit; the -era suffix marks female role; central figure in Philippine melodrama.

records.definition: The person involved in an extramarital affair with a partnered person; the affair partner from the outside.
records.english_term: the other woman / the other man
records.notes: English phrase used directly in Tagalog; 'ang ibang babae/lalaki'; very common in Philippine relationship discourse.

records.definition: Literal: 'outside spouse'; a long-term affair partner maintained almost like a second spouse; the most serious form of kabit relationship.
records.notes: Novel concept: implies sustained parallel relationship with domestic qualities; more serious than casual affair; distinct from kabit's transactional connotation.

records.definition: Literal: 'safe relationship'; ironic euphemism for a secret affair, where 'safe' means hidden from discovery rather than emotionally safe.
records.notes: Novel concept: darkly ironic Philippine phrase; 'ligtas' (safe) refers to safety from being discovered, not from harm.

records.definition: Literal: 'just playing / it's just a game'; dismissive framing used to minimize the significance of an affair or casual sexual relationship.
records.notes: Novel concept: distinctly Filipino rationalization for infidelity; implies affairs are not serious; often said by the cheating party.

records.definition: Temporary; a temporary relationship or arrangement used to describe short-term affairs without commitment.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'panandalian' (temporary) used as noun/descriptor for casual affairs; implies no permanence intended from the start.

records.definition: Literal: 'just for pleasure / only for enjoyment'; justification for engaging in casual sex or affairs without emotional attachment.
records.english_term: just for fun / just for pleasure
records.notes: Novel concept: common Filipino rationalization for casual sex or infidelity; emphasizes transactional pleasure-seeking without commitment.

records.definition: Literal: 'no promise / no commitment'; a stated term for casual sexual relationships with no expectation of a future.
records.notes: Equivalent to NSA; used both in dating profiles and as relationship descriptor; culturally resonant in Philippines.

records.definition: A hidden romantic or sexual partner; someone kept secret from one's spouse, family, or social circle.
records.notes: English phrase used directly in Tagalog; also called 'sikreto' in Tagalog; common in OPM song lyrics.

records.definition: Young unmarried man; the male equivalent of 'dalaga'; implies bachelorhood but without equivalent purity pressure as women.
records.notes: Novel concept: asymmetric counterpart to dalaga; binata status carries far less purity expectation than dalaga; reflects gender double standard.

records.definition: Literal: 'still a virgin'; affirmation of maintained sexual purity; a statement of honor status in Filipino purity culture.
records.notes: Novel concept: the phrase 'pa rin' (still) implies social pressure to maintain virginity despite passing time; contextually significant.

records.definition: Cleanliness; in sexual/moral context, purity of body and character; sexual innocence as a form of cleanliness.
records.notes: Novel concept: kalinisan conflates physical cleanliness with sexual purity in Filipino Catholic moral framework.

records.definition: Purity; absolute moral and sexual innocence; the formal/literary term for pagkadalisay.
records.notes: Novel concept: more formal/literary than pagkadalisay; used in religious and ceremonial contexts.

records.definition: Literal: 'good woman'; a woman who maintains her sexual purity and conforms to conservative sexual norms.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'mabuting babae' encodes sexual purity as moral goodness; a 'good woman' is sexually chaste in Philippine Catholic culture.

records.definition: Literal: 'honorable woman'; a woman whose sexual purity and social comportment brings honor to herself and her family.
records.notes: Novel concept: honor here is explicitly sexual; a woman's honor (dangal) is bound to her sexual status in Filipino culture.

records.definition: Demure, modest, reserved in behavior; the ideal female comportment in conservative Filipino culture, implying sexual restraint.
records.notes: Novel concept: mahinhin is a positive social ideal for Filipino women; the opposite of being 'malandî' (flirtatious/easy).

records.definition: A demure, proper, sexually pure maiden; the ideal combination of modesty (mahinhin) and unmarried status (dalaga).
records.notes: Novel concept: the phrase captures the most prized female status in traditional Filipino Catholic culture.

records.definition: Literal: 'easy to get'; description of a woman perceived as sexually available or promiscuous; shaming term.
records.notes: Gendered shaming phrase; applied almost exclusively to women; equivalent to 'easy' in English slut-shaming contexts.

records.definition: Literal: 'just like that / carelessly'; describes a woman who is sexually available without proper courtship or commitment.
records.notes: Carries judgment about lack of proper sequencing (courtship → commitment → sex); violates Filipino sexual norms.

records.definition: Literal: 'already gave it'; euphemism for a woman who has lost her virginity, with connotation of surrender or concession.
records.notes: The framing as 'giving' implies purity as something a woman possesses and surrenders; deeply embedded in Filipino virginity ideology.

records.definition: Tagalog-English hybrid: 'already gave up / gave in'; refers to a woman having lost her virginity or submitted to sexual pressure.
records.notes: Mixing of 'give up' English with Tagalog grammar; implies virginity loss as capitulation to pressure.

records.definition: Literal: 'not a virgin'; the direct statement of virginity loss; carries significant social shame for Filipino women.
records.notes: Direct factual statement carrying heavy social weight in conservative Filipino context; can destroy a woman's social reputation.

records.definition: Literal: 'purity is already gone'; formal/moral framing of virginity loss as the disappearance of a precious quality.
records.notes: More elevated/formal register than 'hindi birhen'; frames virginity loss as irreversible spiritual/moral loss.

records.definition: Literal: 'already played'; euphemism indicating someone is sexually experienced; has lost their virginity.
records.notes: 'Naglaro' (played) as euphemism for sexual experience; the 'na' indicates completion; implies experience as a taint.

records.definition: Literal: 'already exceeded / already crossed over'; euphemism for having had sex, especially for losing virginity.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'nalagpasan' implies a line/threshold was crossed; framing virginity loss as crossing a point of no return.

records.definition: Literal: 'already freed oneself / liberated oneself'; somewhat positive framing of sexual freedom, contrasting with purity ideology.
records.notes: Novel concept: alternative framing to shame-based virginity loss discourse; used by more progressive Filipinos.

records.definition: Sin; in sexual context, any sexual activity outside of marriage; the fundamental moral-religious concept underlying Filipino sexual conservatism.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'kasalanan' in Filipino Catholic culture specifically includes premarital sex, infidelity, and non-procreative sex as sins.

records.definition: A sinner; in sexual context, someone who has committed sexual sins; applied especially to sexually active unmarried women.
records.notes: Often applied specifically to sexually transgressive women in Filipino Catholic moral discourse.

records.definition: Immorality; typically sexual immorality in Philippine Catholic usage; any violation of sexual moral norms.
records.notes: From Spanish/English; used in formal religious and public discourse to describe sexual transgression.

records.definition: Literal: 'without shame'; used for someone who flaunts social/sexual norms without remorse; the worst social accusation in Filipino shame culture.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'hiya' (shame) is foundational to Filipino social identity; 'walang hiya' is among the harshest social condemnations.

records.definition: Shame-inducing; something or someone that causes shame to their family or community; sexually disgraceful.
records.notes: Novel concept: mapanghiya refers to the social shame caused to family (not just individual); reflects communal honor structure.

records.definition: Immoral; sexually transgressive in the Catholic moral framework; applied to persons, acts, or content.
records.notes: Tagalog adaptation of Spanish/English 'inmoral'; applied to sexually non-conforming behavior; common in media and public discourse.

records.definition: Sexual sin; specifically sexual transgressions classified as sins in Filipino Catholic moral theology.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'sekswal na kasalanan' encompasses premarital sex, adultery, homosexual acts, etc. per Philippine Catholic framework.

records.definition: Literal: 'sin of the body'; Catholic framing of sexual sin as rooted in bodily weakness; carnal sin.
records.notes: Novel concept: specifically locates sin in the physical body as distinct from the soul; Catholic theological framing.

records.definition: Literal: 'flesh and blood'; in sexual/moral context, human carnal weakness; the body's susceptibility to sexual temptation.
records.notes: Novel concept: Filipino Catholic phrase for bodily/sexual weakness; 'laman at dugo' as explanation/excuse for sexual transgression.

records.definition: Devil; in Filipino Catholic sexual discourse, the force causing sexual temptation; a person causing sexual sin can be called 'diablo'.
records.notes: Novel concept: in Philippine sexual morality, sexual temptation is literally attributed to demonic influence; used to excuse or explain sexual transgression.

records.definition: Temptation; specifically sexual temptation in Filipino Catholic moral discourse; also used as verb 'tuksuhin' (to tempt).
records.notes: Novel concept: 'tukso' frames sexual desire as external temptation to be resisted rather than natural drive; fundamental to Philippine sexual guilt culture.

records.definition: Being sexually tempted; experiencing sexual desire framed as succumbing to temptation.
records.notes: The framing of sexual arousal as 'natutukso' (being tempted) reflects Catholic influence on Filipino sexual self-understanding.

records.definition: Literal: 'defilement of the body'; Catholic framing of sexual sin as making the body impure or unclean.
records.notes: Novel concept: specifically positions the body as a temple that can be defiled through sexual transgression; from catechism teaching.

records.definition: Literal: 'filth of the body'; Catholic moral phrase for the spiritual contamination of the body through sexual transgression.
records.notes: Novel concept: bodily filth as spiritual concept; sexual acts render the body spiritually 'dirty' in Philippine Catholic teaching.

records.definition: Worldly; excessively focused on carnal/material pleasures; a person overly given to sexual indulgence.
records.notes: Novel concept: 'makamundo' in Filipino Catholic framing describes someone who prioritizes bodily/sexual pleasure over spiritual life.

records.definition: Dissolute, dissipated; a person who lives carelessly and indulgently, especially regarding sexual excess.
records.notes: Old Tagalog moral term; similar to salaula but specifically implies ongoing habitual sexual excess; somewhat archaic.

records.definition: Direct Latin-origin clinical term for the male external genital organ, identical to international anatomical nomenclature.
records.notes: Standard anatomical term in Turkish medical and educational discourse; universally recognized across all demographics.

records.definition: Turkish rendering of 'phallus'; used in literary criticism, psychoanalytic theory, and art history; carries Freudian symbolic connotations beyond the purely anatomical.
records.notes: More common in academic and cultural writing than in medical contexts; Lacanian and Freudian 'fallus' concept is widely taught in Turkish universities; less clinical than 'penis'.

records.definition: Compound descriptive phrase meaning 'male sexual organ'; used in formal educational, medical, and legal contexts to avoid both the Latin clinical term and cruder slang.
records.notes: Polysyllabic circumlocution preferred in official curricula and public health materials; feels bureaucratic rather than clinical; common in court transcripts and news reporting.

records.definition: Descriptive compound meaning 'male reproductive organ'; frames the penis primarily in terms of its reproductive function rather than sexual pleasure.
records.notes: Reproductive framing typical of biology textbooks; slightly more formal and sterile than 'erkek cinsel organı'; emphasizes procreation over sexuality; preferred in biology education contexts.

records.definition: Euphemism literally meaning 'member'; a polite or archaic substitute for 'penis', drawing on the same linguistic convention as English 'member'.
records.notes: Also the primary Turkish word for organizational membership; the sexual meaning is now dated and may cause confusion in nonsexual contexts; more common in older literary texts than in contemporary speech.

records.definition: Informal descriptive phrase for 'male organ'; a mild euphemism sitting between the fully clinical compound terms and direct slang.
records.notes: Common in mainstream media and news reporting when a clinical but non-vulgar reference is needed; less formal than 'erkek üreme organı' but still entirely acceptable in public discourse.

records.definition: The primary and most vulgar Turkish crude slang term for the penis; extremely offensive in formal or mixed company and among the strongest taboo words in the language.
records.notes: Also functions as a general-purpose intensifier and insult root (e.g. 'siktiret' = fuck off, 'siktir' = fuck you); considered maximally obscene in mainstream Turkish culture; pervasive in informal male speech despite or because of its taboo status.

records.definition: A very common and highly vulgar Turkish slang term for the penis, on par with 'sik' in crudeness and ubiquity in profane speech.
records.notes: Slightly more common than 'sik' in some regional dialects; also serves as a general insult; historically documented in Ottoman-era erotic poetry and folk literature; both terms are near-synonymous in contemporary usage.

records.definition: Slang for the penis derived from the Turkish word for 'reed' or 'cane'; moderately crude, evoking the reed's cylindrical elongated form.
records.notes: Primary meaning is the plant reed; context disambiguates; less taboo than 'sik' or 'yarak' but still impolite in formal settings; the reed metaphor has ancient cross-cultural resonance.

records.definition: Slang for the penis derived from the Turkish word for 'tool' or 'instrument'; a moderately mild euphemism widely used in male colloquial speech.
records.notes: Primary meaning is literally 'tool/instrument/device'; the sexual meaning is contextually understood and widely used without being maximally offensive; appears freely in male locker-room speech.

records.definition: A crude but sometimes playful Turkish slang term for the penis; slightly less maximally taboo than 'sik' or 'yarak' but still strongly impolite.
records.notes: Sometimes used in childish or diminutive registers, comparable to British 'willy'; crudeness level varies considerably with tone and context; the shorter phonology makes it feel more casual than 'yarak'.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'kazık' meaning 'stake', 'post', or 'pile'; implies rigidity and sharpness; also the primary Turkish word for a financial rip-off or swindle.
records.notes: Dual meaning creates frequent double entendres; 'kazığa oturmak' (to sit on a stake) is a vulgar idiom for anal penetration; the swindle meaning dominates in most everyday contexts so disambiguation is required.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'hortum' meaning 'hose' or 'trunk'; implies a long or large organ; also means a tornado or elephant trunk.
records.notes: Size-implying term; 'fil hortumu' (elephant trunk) is the full extended metaphor for a particularly large penis; used primarily in male joking contexts; the meteorological meaning (waterspout/tornado) is now more common in everyday speech.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'şiş' meaning 'skewer' or 'spike'; evokes a pointed penetrative object; the primary meaning is a kebab skewer.
records.notes: Penetrative implication is clear from the primary meaning; the 'şiş kebap' association lends an inadvertently comic register; moderately recognized as penis slang rather than universally known.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'boru' meaning 'pipe' or 'tube'; evokes the hollow cylindrical form; also means a bugle or trumpet.
records.notes: Cylindrical shape metaphor; 'boru çalmak' (playing the bugle/pipe) creates additional double-entendre potential in crude humor; recognized primarily among adults who use colloquial sexual vocabulary.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'kılıç' meaning 'sword'; a metaphor evoking penetrative power and masculine virility; found in classical and modern erotic literature.
records.notes: More literary and poetic than street-level crude; appears in Ottoman-era erotic poetry and folk songs; heroic or warrior connotations lend a somewhat elevated register compared to blunter penis slang.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'sopa' meaning 'stick' or 'club'; implies a blunt, heavy object; the primary meaning is a wooden beating stick.
records.notes: Slightly more aggressive connotation than 'değnek'; 'sopa yemek' (to be beaten with a stick) in some crude contexts acquires sexual meaning; moderately recognized as sexual slang.

records.definition: Slang for penis derived from 'değnek' meaning 'rod' or 'stick'; a straightforward shape metaphor used in moderately crude informal speech.
records.notes: Less commonly used as penis slang than 'sopa'; primary meanings include divining rod and walking stick; recognized primarily among adults who use colloquial sexual vocabulary; less offensive than the core crude terms.

records.definition: Crude slang for penis derived from 'zımba' meaning 'stapler' or 'hole punch'; emphasizes the repetitive thrusting action of penetration over shape.
records.notes: The mechanical punching or stapling motion directly evokes thrusting during intercourse; somewhat niche compared to other penis slang; 'zımbalamak' (to staple) is used crudely as a verb for penetrative sex in some registers.

records.definition: Euphemism for penis derived from 'muz' meaning 'banana'; a widely understood shape-based metaphor used humorously or to avoid cruder terms.
records.notes: The banana is a universal phallic symbol and this euphemism functions identically to English 'banana'; widely used in advertising innuendo, comedy, and informal speech; low offensive impact; recognized by virtually all adults and many children.

records.definition: Childish or infantile term for the penis, used primarily by and with young children; also deployed humorously or with deliberate infantile affect by adults.
records.notes: Universally recognized and standard in child-rearing contexts; when used by adults conveys humor, intimacy, or deliberate infantilization; not offensive; in some regional child-speech may refer generically to the genital area regardless of sex.

records.definition: Euphemism for penis meaning 'manhood' or 'masculinity'; encapsulates both the anatomical organ and the broader concept of masculine virility and potency.
records.notes: Primarily means 'masculinity' or 'manliness' in non-sexual contexts; in sexual contexts functions as a dignified euphemism for the penis; 'erkekliğini kaybetmek' (to lose one's manhood) conflates erectile dysfunction with general emasculation.

records.definition: Niche or humorous slang for a large or engorged penis; derived from 'şişko' meaning 'fat' or 'chubby'; not a standard or widely established term in Turkish sexual vocabulary.
records.notes: Primary meaning of 'şişko' is simply 'fat person'; its use as penis slang is marginal and context-dependent; low recognition specifically as sexual slang; may reference an erect or unusually thick penis; inclusion in lexical surveys of this section suggests subculture or regional attestation.

records.definition: Descriptive euphemism literally meaning 'the long one'; a humorous or coy deictic reference to the penis, foregrounding length as a sexual desirability marker.
records.notes: A phrase rather than a fixed lexical item; used in joking or indirect speech; the participle-noun construction ('olan' = the one that is) is distinctly Turkish syntax; implies admiration of size rather than being a neutral descriptor.

records.definition: Direct Latin-origin clinical term for the vagina, identical to international anatomical nomenclature; used in medical, educational, and public health contexts.
records.notes: Standard anatomical term; increasingly used in mainstream Turkish media and sex education; recognition has grown with increased school-based sex education initiatives in Turkey; considerably less used in everyday colloquial speech than crude alternatives.

records.definition: Latin-derived clinical term for the external female genitalia, used in Turkish medical and educational contexts.
records.notes: Direct Latin loanword; more common in written and medical Turkish than in everyday speech; less widely known than the loanword 'vajina'.

records.definition: Clinical descriptive phrase meaning 'external genital organs,' used in Turkish anatomy and health education to refer to the vulva collectively.
records.notes: A multi-word descriptive phrase rather than a single lexical item; appears in textbooks and health curricula rather than conversation.

records.definition: Native Turkish compound clinical term for the vagina, literally meaning 'birth path' or 'seed road,' emphasizing its role as the birth canal.
records.notes: Preferred native Turkish alternative to the loanword 'vajina' in formal and educational settings; 'döl' means offspring/seed, 'yol' means road/path.

records.definition: Formal Turkish phrase meaning 'female sexual organ,' used as a general clinical reference to the external and internal female genitalia collectively.
records.notes: Generic and imprecise; covers the entire female genital system rather than a specific structure; common in news media and conservative formal discourse where more specific terms are avoided.

records.definition: Clinical Turkish phrase meaning 'female reproductive organ,' referring broadly to the female reproductive system including vagina, uterus, and ovaries.
records.notes: Emphasizes reproductive function rather than sexual pleasure; used in biology education and conservative health discourse; less precise than anatomical terms.

records.definition: The primary and most taboo Turkish crude slang term for the vagina and vulva; one of the most offensive words in the language.
records.notes: Equivalent in social taboo to English 'cunt'; root for 'amcık', 'am başı', 'amcıklık', and many compound insults; using it in public or mixed company is considered highly offensive.

records.definition: Diminutive form of 'am'; crude slang for the vagina, slightly softened by the diminutive suffix '-cık' but still highly offensive.
records.notes: The diminutive suffix adds a mildly childlike or affectionate register without substantially reducing offensiveness; also functions as a general insult for a cowardly or weak person, parallel to English 'pussy'.

records.definition: Crude slang for the vulva, literally meaning 'crack' or 'slit,' referencing the cleft appearance of the external female genitalia.
records.notes: Literal primary meaning is 'crack' or 'split' (e.g., in wood or stone); the sexual sense is widely understood; slightly less taboo than 'am' because the literal meaning provides surface deniability.

records.definition: Crude slang for the vaginal opening or vulva, literally meaning 'hole'; also applied to the anus in crude speech depending on context.
records.notes: Context-dependent; can refer to the vagina or anus; dehumanizing when applied to a person as a metonym; primary literal meaning is any physical hole or aperture.

records.definition: Colloquial slang for the vulva or mons pubis, literally meaning 'roof' or 'ridge,' possibly referencing the elevated topography of the pubic mound.
records.notes: Less common than primary crude terms; may have regional or generational distribution; the roof metaphor plausibly references the arched prominence of the mons pubis.

records.definition: Euphemistic slang for the vagina using the word 'cat,' directly parallel to English 'pussy'; softer than direct crude terms.
records.notes: Direct structural parallel to English 'pussy'; the animal euphemism provides plausible deniability; may be reinforced by English-language internet and media influence on younger Turkish speakers.

records.definition: Slang for the vagina, literally meaning 'cave,' emphasizing the internal cavity through spatial metaphor.
records.notes: Cave metaphors for the vagina are attested across many languages; implies depth and enclosure; moderately crude depending on context of use.

records.definition: Slang for the vagina, literally meaning 'chest' or 'box,' framing the female genitalia as a container or receptacle.
records.notes: A 'sandık' is a traditional Turkish wooden chest; the container metaphor parallels English 'box'; has an old-fashioned or rural register and is less common in urban speech.

records.definition: Gentle euphemism for the vulva or vagina, literally meaning 'flower'; used in soft, romantic, or indirect contexts.
records.notes: Flower metaphors for female genitalia are widespread cross-linguistically; low taboo level makes it usable in contexts where direct terms would be unacceptable; also used in children's contexts to name genitalia without crude language.

records.definition: Slang for the vagina, literally meaning 'plug,' invoking an electrical plug-and-socket metaphor for penetrative sex in which the vagina is the receptacle.
records.notes: Structurally counter-intuitive since 'fiş' is technically the male plug end in Turkish electrical terminology while 'priz' (socket/outlet) would be the apt female metaphor; recognition as vagina-specific slang is limited and the usage may be niche or regional.

records.definition: Colloquial slang for the vulva, literally meaning 'bundle' or 'cloth-wrapped package,' suggesting the folded appearance of the labia.
records.notes: A 'bohça' is a traditional Turkish cloth used to wrap and carry goods; the metaphor may reference the folded, layered appearance of the labia majora; less common than primary slang terms; possibly more regional or generational.

records.definition: Primary crude Turkish slang for the buttocks or anus; in maximally crude speech occasionally used loosely to refer to female genitalia or the entire posterior genital-anal region.
records.notes: Primary and overwhelmingly dominant meaning is buttocks/anus, not vagina; listed in the vagina-slang category because some crude speakers use it interchangeably for all female posterior anatomy; one of the highest-frequency crude terms in Turkish.

records.definition: Turkish loanword for the labia, referring collectively to the labia majora and labia minora of the vulva; used in medical and health education contexts.
records.notes: Direct borrowing from Latin anatomical terminology via French or English; functions generically covering both structures; 'labya majora' and 'labya minora' are the specified forms used when precision is required.

records.definition: Crude compound term for the labia, literally 'lip of the am (vagina),' combining the primary crude term for vagina with the word for lip.
records.notes: The crude root 'am' elevates the taboo level substantially above neutral anatomical equivalents; used in crude speech and pornographic contexts; refers to the labia generically, most commonly evoking the inner lips (minora) as the more visually prominent.

records.definition: Clinical Turkish term for the labia minora, literally meaning 'small lip'; the native Turkish translation of the Latin anatomical term.
records.notes: Used in Turkish medical textbooks and health education as the preferred native alternative to 'labya minora'; a transparent descriptive compound with no crude connotations.

records.definition: Clinical Turkish term for the labia majora, literally meaning 'large lip'; the native Turkish translation of the Latin anatomical term.
records.notes: Used in Turkish medical textbooks and health education as the preferred native alternative to 'labya majora'; a transparent descriptive compound with no crude connotations.

records.definition: Clinical Turkish descriptive term for the labia minora, literally 'inner lip,' emphasizing anatomical position rather than relative size.
records.notes: Alternative framing to 'küçük dudak' (small lip); uses the inner/outer spatial distinction rather than the small/large size distinction; both framings appear in Turkish anatomy instruction.

records.definition: Clinical Turkish descriptive term for the labia majora, literally 'outer lip,' emphasizing anatomical position rather than relative size.
records.notes: Alternative framing to 'büyük dudak' (large lip); uses the inner/outer spatial distinction rather than the large/small size distinction; paired with 'iç dudak' as a complementary anatomical set.

records.definition: Turkish loanword for the clitoris, the primary female organ of sexual pleasure at the anterior junction of the labia minora.
records.notes: Direct borrowing from Greek/Latin anatomical terminology; dominant term in Turkish medical and sexual health education; awareness may be lower in older and rural populations due to historical suppression of female sexuality education in Turkey.

records.definition: Crude compound term for the clitoris or its glans, literally 'head of the am (vagina),' structurally paralleling the anatomical concept of the glans penis.
records.notes: Combines the crude root 'am' with 'baş' (head), creating a structural parallel to 'penis başı' (glans penis); the crude rating derives primarily from the 'am' root rather than from the concept itself; specifically evokes the visible external tip rather than the full clitoral complex.

records.definition: Clinical circumlocution for the clitoris, using the general Turkish word for 'gland' or 'nodule.'
records.notes: 'Beze' ordinarily means 'gland' or 'lymph node'; its application to the clitoris is a medical circumlocution rather than a dedicated anatomical term.

records.definition: Euphemistic anatomical metaphor for the clitoris, literally meaning 'little hill' or 'little mound.'
records.notes: Descriptive topographic metaphor; not a standard medical term and rarely used outside informal or health-education contexts.

records.definition: Clinical term for the testicle; a direct Latin loanword used in Turkish medical and educational contexts.
records.notes: Standard anatomical term in Turkish medicine; the Turkish plural is 'testisler.'

records.definition: Clinical plural form of 'testis,' the Latin-origin Turkish word for the testicles.
records.notes: Formed by applying the standard Turkish plural suffix -ler to the loanword 'testis.'

records.definition: Clinical term for the scrotum; a direct Latin loanword used in Turkish medical contexts.
records.notes: Less commonly encountered than 'testis' in everyday Turkish; primarily confined to medical and educational usage.

records.definition: Archaic Arabic-origin Turkish term for the testicle, found in Ottoman texts and classical dictionaries.
records.notes: Borrowed from Arabic 'khusya' (خصية); largely displaced in modern Turkish by 'testis' (clinical) and 'taşak' (slang); still appears in literary and religious texts.

records.definition: Clinical descriptive phrase for the testicle, literally meaning 'male reproductive gland.'
records.notes: A phrase-level circumlocution rather than a dedicated anatomical noun; used in health education materials to avoid both crude slang and unfamiliar loanwords.

records.definition: The dominant crude slang term for testicle(s) in Turkish, widely used in profanity and insults.
records.notes: One of the most common sexual insults in Turkish; appears in high-frequency expletive compounds like 'taşağını yerim'; also used metaphorically for courage, parallel to English 'balls.'

records.definition: Slang term for testicles, literally meaning 'egg(s),' referring to the ovoid shape of the testes.
records.notes: Parallel to English colloquial 'eggs' for testicles; widely understood but less vulgar than 'taşak'; primary meaning of the word is chicken egg, making the sexual meaning entirely contextual.

records.definition: Slang term for testicle(s), literally meaning 'ball,' used analogously to English 'ball' for the testes.
records.notes: Primary meaning of 'top' in Turkish is 'ball' (sporting implement); the sexual meaning is contextual and widely understood but not the default reading of the word.

records.definition: Dated Arabic-origin Turkish slang for testicle, homophonous with the Arabic word for 'shame' or 'modesty.'
records.notes: Homophonous with 'haya' (Arabic hayā, meaning shame/modesty), creating an unintentional semantic resonance between genitalia and shame; declining in everyday use but still found in rural and older-generation speech.

records.definition: Slang term for testicle, literally meaning 'bell,' referring to the pendant rounded shape of the testes.
records.notes: Less widespread than 'taşak' or 'yumurta'; the bell metaphor parallels similar shape-based anatomical slang in other languages.

records.definition: Crude slang for testicle(s), literally meaning 'mallet' or 'club,' emphasizing weight and mass.
records.notes: The same word is also applied to the penis in some regional dialects, causing contextual ambiguity; in the testicles sense it evokes heaviness rather than the egg or ball metaphors.

records.definition: Slang term for the scrotum, literally meaning 'bag' or 'sack,' referring to its pouch-like structure.
records.notes: Parallel to English 'sack' or 'bag' for the scrotum; primarily designates the scrotal pouch rather than the testes themselves, though speakers often use it loosely for both.

records.definition: Clinical term for the anus; a direct Latin loanword used in Turkish medical and educational contexts.
records.notes: Standard anatomical term; widely recognized due to health education campaigns, though many speakers prefer colloquial alternatives in casual speech.

records.definition: Formal Arabic-origin Turkish term for the anus, used in medical, legal, and forensic contexts.
records.notes: Borrowed from Arabic 'maq'ad' (مقعد, seat/buttocks); in Turkish it denotes the anus specifically; found in court documents, forensic reports, and Islamic jurisprudence texts; declining as 'anüs' becomes the standard clinical term.

records.definition: Clinical term for the rectum, the terminal segment of the large intestine; a direct Latin loanword.
records.notes: Confined primarily to medical and anatomical contexts; less commonly known than 'anüs' among the general public; recognition limited largely to those with medical education or interest.

records.definition: Clinical descriptive phrase for the anal opening, literally meaning 'anal aperture.'
records.notes: A phrase-level clinical description used in health education and medical documentation rather than a dedicated anatomical noun; 'anal' is a Latin-origin loanword in Turkish.

records.definition: The primary and most vulgar Turkish slang word for the anus and buttocks, equivalent to English 'ass' or 'arse.'
records.notes: Extremely common expletive and insult; functions as both a body-part term and a general intensifier; central to a large family of Turkish profanity including compound insults; one of the highest-frequency vulgarisms in spoken Turkish.

records.definition: Crude-to-neutral slang for the buttocks, less vulgar than 'göt' but still informal.
records.notes: Primary meaning is 'buttocks' rather than anus specifically; used loosely for both; less offensive than 'göt' and acceptable in some informal registers; also the nautical term for the stern of a ship.

records.definition: Childish or polite euphemism for the buttocks, used with young children and in informal polite contexts.
records.notes: Reduplicated form typical of baby-talk registers; used by parents with young children and in polite conversation to avoid crude terms; not specific to the anus.

records.definition: Very crude compound slang for the anus, literally meaning 'shit hole.'
records.notes: 'Bok' = excrement/shit; 'delik' = hole; the compound is maximally vulgar and serves both as an anatomical reference and a strong general insult, parallel to English 'shithole.'

records.definition: Generic euphemism for the anus, literally meaning 'hole,' used to avoid naming the anatomy directly.
records.notes: Primary meaning is simply 'hole' (any aperture); sexual meaning depends entirely on context; frequently appears in sexual slang phrases such as 'deliğine sokmak' (to insert into the hole).

records.definition: Polite euphemism for the buttocks or rear end, literally meaning 'back side' or 'rear part.'
records.notes: Used to refer to the buttocks without vulgarity; not specific to the anus; parallel to English 'backside' or 'rear end'; suitable in polite conversation.

records.definition: Slang term for the anus, literally meaning 'ring,' referring to the circular shape of the anal sphincter.
records.notes: Primary meaning of 'yüzük' is 'finger ring' (jewelry); the sexual meaning exploits the circular shape analogy; parallel to British slang 'ring' for the anus; recognized in sexual contexts but not a dominant term.

records.definition: Literally 'its back/behind'; a common Turkish euphemism for the anus in sexual contexts.
records.notes: The possessive suffix -sı makes it 'its back'; works as a euphemism by naming the general region rather than the specific orifice.

records.definition: The standard Turkish word for breast or mammary gland, used in clinical, everyday, and breastfeeding contexts.
records.notes: Primary lexical item for the organ in Turkish; not vulgar but gains sexual charge in explicitly sexual contexts.

records.definition: Chest or breast; the primary anatomical term for the thoracic region, commonly referring to female breasts in sexual contexts.
records.notes: More general than 'meme' — covers the entire chest wall; meaning shifts to specifically female breasts in sexual discourse.

records.definition: Literally 'woman's breast'; an explicit clinical or descriptive compound phrase specifying the female mammary gland.
records.notes: Compound phrase rather than a single lexical item; used in medical or instructional contexts to distinguish female breast tissue.

records.definition: Loanword from French/English 'bust'; refers to the chest and breast region, often emphasizing shape or measurement.
records.notes: Primarily used in fashion, bra sizing, and aesthetic contexts; less explicitly sexual than 'meme'.

records.definition: Literally 'breast head/tip'; the standard Turkish anatomical term for the nipple.
records.notes: Compound noun; 'başı' means 'its head'. Standard non-euphemistic word for the nipple in Turkish.

records.definition: Literally 'balloon'; crude slang for large, round female breasts.
records.notes: Metaphor emphasizes size and roundness; used humorously or lewdly; most effective when applied to notably large breasts.

records.definition: Literally 'ball'; crude slang for female breasts, emphasizing their round shape.
records.notes: Usually used in plural (toplar) when referring to both breasts; same shape metaphor as English 'balls' applied to breasts.

records.definition: Literally 'round'; used as playful or mild slang for female breasts, relying on shape as the metonym.
records.notes: Less immediately vulgar than 'top' or 'balon'; highly context-dependent — the word means round in all other uses, so the sexual reading requires unambiguous framing.

records.definition: Literally 'breast tip'; a colloquial Turkish term for the nipple, slightly more visual and descriptive than 'meme başı'.

records.definition: Literally 'baby bottle' (from French biberon); playful slang for female breasts or nipples, exploiting the feeding association.

records.definition: Literally 'stone/rock'; crude slang for firm, hard female breasts.

records.definition: Literally 'watermelon'; crude slang for large female breasts, emphasizing their size and round shape.
records.notes: Classic Turkish food-based size metaphor; directly parallels English 'melons'. Widely understood and used humorously or lewdly.

records.definition: Literally 'sexual relationship/connection'; the standard Turkish clinical term for sexual intercourse.
records.notes: 'cinsel' (sexual) + 'ilişki' (relationship/contact); default neutral term in health education, legal contexts, and broadcast media.

records.definition: Direct borrowing of Latin 'coitus'; restricted to medical, academic, and sexological usage in Turkish.

records.definition: Borrowing of English/Latin 'copulation'; used in biology, zoology, and academic sexology in Turkish.
records.notes: Rarer than 'koitus' in everyday Turkish; primarily appears in scientific or academic texts; applying it to humans carries a dehumanizing register.

records.definition: Literally 'coupling/mating'; a clinical-register Turkish term for sexual intercourse, most commonly applied to animal reproduction in biological contexts.
records.notes: From 'çift' (pair/couple) + '-leşme' (becoming); when applied to humans can sound clinical, humorous, or mildly dehumanizing due to primary use in animal biology.

records.definition: Literally 'union/joining'; a euphemistic Turkish term for sexual intercourse emphasizing the act of two bodies merging.
records.notes: 'Birleşme' has many non-sexual meanings (political merger, physical junction); the sexual sense is derived entirely from context; common in literary or romantic framing.

records.definition: Direct borrowing of 'penetration'; used in medical, psychological, and sexological contexts to describe entry into a bodily orifice.
records.notes: Recognition higher among educated urban populations; primarily encountered in clinical or educational texts rather than everyday speech.

records.definition: The primary Turkish taboo verb for sexual intercourse, directly equivalent to English 'to fuck' in both sexual and general expletive uses.

records.definition: Reciprocal form of 'sikmek'; means to fuck each other or have sex mutually, framing intercourse as a shared act between participants.

records.definition: Crude slang for sexual intercourse implying an active and dominant role; slightly less intense than 'sikmek' but still highly vulgar.

records.definition: Literally 'to level/flatten'; crude slang for sexual intercourse implying the active penetrating role.

records.definition: Literally 'to strike/spark/click'; used as crude slang for sexual intercourse, analogous to English 'to bang' or 'to hit'.

records.definition: Crude Turkish slang for penetrative intercourse, literally 'to dip/plunge into.'

records.definition: Crude Turkish slang for having sex, literally 'to dig,' evoking aggressive repetitive thrusting.

records.definition: Crude Turkish slang for vigorous intercourse, literally 'to mince/grind (meat).'

records.definition: Crude Turkish slang for penetrative sex, literally 'to stretch,' emphasizing the physical dilation of the receptive partner.

records.definition: Crude Turkish slang for rubbing genitals against a partner, literally 'to rub/grind'; covers both non-penetrative frottage and is used loosely for sex generally.

records.definition: Very crude Turkish slang for having sex forcefully; possibly onomatopoeic or derived from 'bomba' (bomb).

records.definition: Crude Turkish phrase for anal sex, incorporating British English loanword 'bum' (buttocks) plus Turkish 'yapmak' (to do).

records.definition: Turkish euphemism for sexual intercourse, literally 'to do'; the sexual meaning is entirely context-dependent.

records.definition: Crude Turkish slang for having sex, literally 'to push/shove against each other (reciprocally).'

records.definition: Turkish phonological adaptation of Latin/English 'fellatio'; oral stimulation of the penis.

records.definition: Turkish loanword calque of English 'oral sex'; covers both fellatio and cunnilingus.

records.definition: Formal Turkish clinical phrase for oral sex, literally 'oral sexual intercourse/relation.'

records.definition: Highly formal Turkish clinical phrase for fellatio, literally 'oral stimulation on/upon the penis.'

records.definition: The dominant Turkish crude slang term for a blowjob/fellatio.

records.definition: Turkish slang for oral sex (fellatio or cunnilingus), literally 'to lick.'

records.definition: Turkish crude slang for fellatio, literally 'to suck.'

records.definition: Turkish euphemism for oral sex, literally 'mouth job/work.'
records.notes: Structurally parallel to 'el işi' (handcraft/needlework); serves as a discreet substitute for 'sakso' in contexts requiring some delicacy; gender-neutral — applicable to fellatio or cunnilingus.

records.definition: Truncated Turkish crude slang for fellatio; short form of 'sakso' or possibly an independent term.

records.definition: Turkish humorous euphemism for fellatio, literally 'to play the flute/whistle.'

records.definition: Turkish humorous/euphemistic slang for fellatio, literally 'to chirp or sing (as a bird does).'

records.definition: Turkish slang/euphemism for fellatio with implied swallowing, literally 'to drink.'

records.definition: Turkish phonological adaptation of 'cunnilingus'; oral stimulation of the female genitalia.

records.definition: Latin/English clinical term used as an unadapted loanword in Turkish for oral stimulation of the female genitalia.

records.definition: Crude verb phrase meaning 'to eat the cunt'; uses the diminutive 'amcık' of 'am' and the verb 'yemek' (to eat).

records.definition: Polysemous verb meaning 'to eat'; used in sexual slang to mean performing cunnilingus, parallel to English 'eating out'.

records.definition: Euphemistic phrase meaning 'to go down'; used for performing oral sex on a partner, structurally borrowed from English 'go down on'.

records.definition: Slang phrase meaning 'to do a dive'; used for performing cunnilingus, evoking the image of plunging one's face into the genitals.

records.definition: Loanword from French/English 'masturbation'; the standard clinical Turkish term for self-stimulation of the genitals.

records.definition: Clinical term for autoeroticism; self-directed sexual arousal and activity, encompassing masturbation and fantasy.

records.definition: Euphemistic phrase meaning 'manual satisfaction'; a polite circumlocution for masturbation.

records.definition: Verb phrase meaning 'to masturbate'; combines the loanword stem 'mastürbe' with the auxiliary 'olmak' (to become/be).

records.definition: The number 'thirty-one' repurposed as the dominant Turkish slang for masturbation; the digits 3 and 1 together visually suggest a hand holding a penis.

records.definition: Spelled-out variant of '31 çekmek', writing 'thirty-one pull' in full; functionally identical to the numeral form.

records.definition: Verb meaning 'to stroke or smooth'; used in slang for masturbation, emphasizing the stroking motion.

records.definition: Verb meaning 'to pull'; used as standalone crude slang for masturbation, shorthand extracted from '31 çekmek'.

records.definition: Verb meaning 'to cup or grip with the palm'; used as slang for masturbation, emphasizing the gripping action around the penis.

records.definition: Euphemistic phrase meaning 'self-satisfaction'; a polite or clinical circumlocution for masturbation.

records.definition: Agent noun from 'otuzbir'; literally 'a thirty-one-er', meaning a person who masturbates; also used pejoratively for a useless, idle, or contemptible person.

records.definition: Loanword compound for anal sex; the standard clinical and colloquial Turkish term for sexual activity involving the anus.

records.definition: Clinical phrase meaning 'anal intercourse'; 'ilişki' is the standard Turkish word for both 'relationship' and 'intercourse'.

records.definition: Highly technical clinical term meaning 'anal copulation'; used in academic sexology and forensic medicine.

records.definition: Clinical phrase meaning 'anal penetration'; specifies insertion into the anus without specifying the penetrating body part.

records.definition: Extremely crude verb phrase meaning 'to fuck in the ass'; uses 'göt' (ass) with ablative suffix and 'sikmek', the most vulgar Turkish copulatory verb.

records.definition: Crude Turkish phrasal verb meaning to be the receptive partner in anal sex; literally 'to give ass.'

records.definition: Crude Turkish phrase meaning to receive anal penetration; literally 'to take it from the ass.'

records.definition: Turkish phrase meaning to receive anal penetration; literally 'to take/receive from behind.'

records.definition: Turkish crude phrase for anal penetration from the active/insertive role; literally 'to enter from behind.'
records.notes: 'Girmek' (to enter) unambiguously marks the active/penetrating role; 'arkadan' (from behind) implies anal rather than vaginal entry in context; no specific anal_sex_active concept exists in registry so mapped to general anal_sex.

records.definition: Turkish Islamic jurisprudence term for anal intercourse, borrowed from Arabic 'liwāṭ'; used in religious and historical-legal discourse condemning same-sex anal acts.
records.notes: From Arabic liwāṭ (لواط), derived from the Prophet Lot (Lūṭ) narrative; appears in Ottoman criminal law and Islamic fiqh; not used in colloquial speech; recognition declining as religious-legal vocabulary recedes.

records.definition: Turkish clinical loanword from English 'orgasm'; the climax of sexual excitement marked by intense pleasure and rhythmic muscular contractions.
